#!/bin/bash # JMeter Performance Test Execution Script # This script runs JMeter tests and generates comprehensive reports # Configuration JMETER_HOME="/opt/apache-jmeter-5.5" TEST_PLAN="api-performance-test.jmx" RESULTS_DIR="results/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)" REPORT_DIR="$RESULTS_DIR/report" LOG_FILE="$RESULTS_DIR/jmeter.log" # Create results directory mkdir -p $RESULTS_DIR $REPORT_DIR # Environment variables for test export TEST_ENV="staging" export USERS=1000 export RAMP_UP=300 export DURATION=1800 echo "Starting JMeter performance test..." echo "Test Plan: $TEST_PLAN" echo "Users: $USERS" echo "Ramp Up: $RAMP_UP seconds" echo "Duration: $DURATION seconds" echo "Results Directory: $RESULTS_DIR" # Run JMeter in non-GUI mode $JMETER_HOME/bin/jmeter \ -n \ # Non-GUI mode -t $TEST_PLAN \ # Test plan file -l $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ # Results file -j $LOG_FILE \ # Log file -e \ # Generate report dashboard -o $REPORT_DIR \ # Report output directory -Jusers=$USERS \ # Number of users -Jrampup=$RAMP_UP \ # Ramp-up period -Jduration=$DURATION \ # Test duration -Jtest.data.dir="test-data" \ # Test data directory -Jreport.dir=$RESULTS_DIR # Report directory # Check exit code if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then echo "JMeter test completed successfully" else echo "JMeter test failed. Check logs: $LOG_FILE" exit 1 fi # Generate additional reports echo "\nGenerating additional reports..." # 1. Generate CSV summary report $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --generate-csv $RESULTS_DIR/summary.csv \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type AggregateReport # 2. Generate response times over time $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --generate-csv $RESULTS_DIR/response_times.csv \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type ResponseTimesOverTime # 3. Generate transactions per second $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --generate-csv $RESULTS_DIR/throughput.csv \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type TransactionsPerSecond # 4. Generate latency percentiles $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --generate-csv $RESULTS_DIR/latency_percentiles.csv \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type LatenciesOverTime # 5. Generate active threads over time $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --generate-csv $RESULTS_DIR/active_threads.csv \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type ThreadsStateOverTime # 6. Generate response codes $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --generate-csv $RESULTS_DIR/response_codes.csv \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type ResponseCodesPerSecond # Analyze results and generate summary echo "\nAnalyzing test results..." # Extract key metrics using JMeter's JMESPath-like queries METRICS_FILE="$RESULTS_DIR/key_metrics.txt" cat > $METRICS_FILE << EOF === PERFORMANCE TEST RESULTS SUMMARY === Test Date: $(date) Test Duration: $DURATION seconds Concurrent Users: $USERS KEY METRICS: EOF # Use JTL analyzer to get metrics $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --tool Reporter \ --generate-report \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type AggregateReport \ | grep -A 20 "Overall" >> $METRICS_FILE echo "\n=== ERROR ANALYSIS ===" >> $METRICS_FILE $JMETER_HOME/bin/JMeterPluginsCMD.sh \ --tool Reporter \ --generate-report \ --input-jtl $RESULTS_DIR/results.jtl \ --plugin-type ErrorsPerSecond \ | tail -20 >> $METRICS_FILE # Check SLAs and generate pass/fail report SLA_FILE="$RESULTS_DIR/sla_validation.txt" cat > $SLA_FILE << EOF === SLA VALIDATION REPORT === SLA Requirements: - 95th percentile response time < 500ms - Error rate < 1% - Throughput > 100 requests/second Actual Results: EOF # Extract actual metrics (simplified - in reality you'd parse the CSV) # This is a placeholder for actual metric extraction logic echo "95th Percentile: 423ms [PASS]" >> $SLA_FILE echo "Error Rate: 0.2% [PASS]" >> $SLA_FILE echo "Throughput: 245 requests/second [PASS]" >> $SLA_FILE # Create a simple HTML report HTML_REPORT="$RESULTS_DIR/test_summary.html" cat > $HTML_REPORT << EOF Performance Test Report

API Performance Test Report

Test Summary

Test Date: $(date)

Duration: $DURATION seconds

Concurrent Users: $USERS

Environment: $TEST_ENV

Key Metrics

Metric Value SLA Status
95th Percentile Response Time 423ms < 500ms PASS
Error Rate 0.2% < 1% PASS
Throughput 245 req/sec > 100 req/sec PASS
Average Response Time 215ms < 300ms PASS

Report Files

  • HTML Dashboard
  • Raw Results (JTL)
  • Summary CSV
  • Response Times CSV
  • Throughput CSV

Recommendations

  • Database connection pool can be increased from 50 to 100 connections
  • Add caching for product catalog API responses
  • Consider implementing API rate limiting for admin endpoints
EOF echo "\nTest execution completed!" echo "Results available in: $RESULTS_DIR" echo "HTML Report: $RESULTS_DIR/test_summary.html" echo "Dashboard: $REPORT_DIR/index.html" # Optional: Upload results to monitoring system # curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @$RESULTS_DIR/summary.csv https://monitoring.example.com/api/results # Optional: Send notification # echo "Performance test completed. Results: $RESULTS_DIR" | mail -s "Performance Test Results" team@example.com

content.title: Advanced JMeter Techniques
content.explanation:
**Distributed Testing**:
Run tests from multiple machines to generate massive load:
```bash
# On master machine
jmeter -n -t test.jmx -R slave1,slave2,slave3 -l results.jtl

# On slave machines
jmeter-server -Jserver.rmi.ssl.disable=true
```

**Cloud Execution with BlazeMeter**:
Scale tests beyond your infrastructure:
```yaml
# blazemeter.yaml
test:
  name: "API Load Test"
  runtime:
    executor: "jmeter"
    concurrency: 1000
    ramp-up: 5m
    hold-for: 30m
  scenarios:
    api-test:
      script: "api-test.jmx"
  reporting:
    - module: "passfail"
      criteria:
        - avg-rt>200ms for 1m, stop as failed
```

**Custom Plugins Development**:
Extend JMeter with Java:
```java
public class CustomSampler extends AbstractJavaSamplerClient {
    @Override
    public SampleResult runTest(JavaSamplerContext context) {
        SampleResult result = new SampleResult();
        result.sampleStart();
        
        // Custom logic here
        
        result.sampleEnd();
        result.setSuccessful(true);
        return result;
    }
}
```

**Correlation Patterns**:
Handle dynamic values like CSRF tokens, session IDs:
```groovy
// Extract from JSON response
def json = new groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(prev.getResponseDataAsString())
vars.put("authToken", json.token)

// Extract from HTML response
import org.jsoup.Jsoup
def doc = Jsoup.parse(prev.getResponseDataAsString())
vars.put("csrfToken", doc.select("input[name=csrf_token]").val())
```

content.title: k6: The Developer-Centric Load Testing Tool
content.explanation:
k6 represents a paradigm shift in load testing - designed for developers with code-first approach:

**Key Features**:
• **JavaScript/TypeScript based**: Tests are code, version-controlled
• **Built-in metrics**: No plugins needed for essential metrics
• **Cloud-native**: Built for CI/CD and cloud execution
• **Resource efficient**: Single binary, low memory footprint
• **Real browser included**: Can drive browser for E2E load testing

**Architecture**:
1. **VUs (Virtual Users)**: Lightweight goroutines, not OS threads
2. **Options object**: Configure stages, thresholds, tags
3. **Default function**: Test execution logic
4. **Setup/Teardown**: For test initialization and cleanup
5. **Lifecycle hooks**: init(), setup(), default(), teardown()

**When to Choose k6**:
• Developer-friendly teams
• CI/CD integration is crucial
• Need modern JavaScript ecosystem
• Want cloud execution (k6 Cloud)
• Need both API and browser testing

content.title: Gatling: High-Performance Load Testing
content.explanation:
Gatling is built for performance engineers who need maximum efficiency and detailed reporting:

**Key Differentiators**:
• **Scala DSL**: Type-safe, expressive test definitions
• **Async Architecture**: Non-blocking I/O, high efficiency
• **Detailed Reports**: Beautiful HTML reports with charts
• **Recorder**: GUI for recording browser sessions
• **Enterprise Features**: Team collaboration, CI/CD integration

**Gatling vs JMeter vs k6**:
• **Performance**: Gatling > k6 > JMeter (in resource efficiency)
• **Learning Curve**: JMeter < k6 < Gatling
• **Reporting**: Gatling > JMeter > k6 (out of the box)
• **CI/CD**: k6 > Gatling > JMeter
• **Protocol Support**: JMeter > Gatling > k6

**When to Choose Gatling**:
• Need maximum performance from load generators
• Require beautiful, detailed reports
• Have Scala/Java expertise on team
• Testing high-throughput systems (>10k RPS)

// ApiPerformanceSimulation.scala
package simulations

import io.gatling.core.Predef._
import io.gatling.http.Predef._
import scala.concurrent.duration._

class ApiPerformanceSimulation extends Simulation {
  
  // HTTP configuration
  val httpProtocol = http
    .baseUrl("https://api.example.com")
    .acceptHeader("application/json")
    .acceptEncodingHeader("gzip, deflate")
    .userAgentHeader("Gatling Performance Test")
    .shareConnections
    .disableCaching
    .maxConnectionsPerHost(100)
  
  // Headers
  val jsonHeaders = Map(
    "Content-Type" -> "application/json",
    "Accept" -> "application/json"
  )
  
  // Feeder for test data (could also use CSV)
  val userFeeder = Iterator.continually(Map(
    "username" -> ("user" + java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString.take(8)),
    "password" -> "Test@123",
    "email" -> ("test" + java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString.take(8) + "@example.com")
  ))
  
  val productFeeder = csv("data/products.csv").random
  
  // Scenarios
  object Authentication {
    val login = exec(
      http("Login API")
        .post("/api/v1/auth/login")
        .headers(jsonHeaders)
        .body(StringBody(
          """{
            "username": "${username}",
            "password": "${password}"
          }"""
        ))
        .check(status.is(200))
        .check(jsonPath("$.token").saveAs("authToken"))
        .check(jsonPath("$.user.id").saveAs("userId"))
    ).pause(1.second, 3.seconds)
  }
  
  object Products {
    val browse = exec(
      http("Browse Products")
        .get("/api/v1/products")
        .queryParam("category", "${category}")
        .queryParam("page", "1")
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${authToken}")
        .check(status.is(200))
        .check(jsonPath("$.products[0].id").optional.saveAs("firstProductId"))
    ).pause(2.seconds, 5.seconds)
    
    val viewProduct = exec(
      http("View Product Details")
        .get("/api/v1/products/${productId}")
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${authToken}")
        .check(status.is(200))
        .check(jsonPath("$.name").exists)
    ).pause(1.second, 2.seconds)
  }
  
  object Checkout {
    val addToCart = exec(
      http("Add to Cart")
        .post("/api/v1/cart/items")
        .headers(jsonHeaders)
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${authToken}")
        .body(StringBody(
          """{
            "productId": "${productId}",
            "quantity": 1
          }"""
        ))
        .check(status.is(201))
    ).pause(1.second)
    
    val checkout = exec(
      http("Checkout")
        .post("/api/v1/checkout")
        .headers(jsonHeaders)
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${authToken}")
        .body(StringBody(
          """{
            "paymentMethod": "credit_card",
            "shippingAddress": {
              "street": "123 Main St",
              "city": "San Francisco",
              "zipCode": "94105"
            }
          }"""
        ))
        .check(status.is(200))
        .check(jsonPath("$.orderId").saveAs("orderId"))
    ).pause(2.seconds)
  }
  
  object Admin {
    val viewStats = exec(
      http("Admin Statistics")
        .get("/api/v1/admin/stats")
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${authToken}")
        .header("X-Admin-Token", "${adminToken}")
        .check(status.is(200))
    ).pause(5.seconds, 10.seconds)
  }
  
  // Define scenarios
  val browsingScenario = scenario("Browsing Users")
    .feed(userFeeder)
    .exec(Authentication.login)
    .feed(productFeeder)
    .during(5.minutes) {
      exec(Products.browse)
        .exec(Products.viewProduct)
        .pause(10.seconds, 30.seconds)
    }
  
  val purchasingScenario = scenario("Purchasing Users")
    .feed(userFeeder)
    .exec(Authentication.login)
    .feed(productFeeder)
    .exec(Products.browse)
    .exec(Checkout.addToCart)
    .exec(Checkout.checkout)
    .pause(1.minute)
  
  val adminScenario = scenario("Admin Users")
    .feed(userFeeder)
    .exec(Authentication.login)
    .exec(Admin.viewStats)
    .pause(2.minutes)
    .repeat(5) {
      exec(Admin.viewStats)
        .pause(30.seconds)
    }
  
  // Setup simulation
  setUp(
    browsingScenario.inject(
      nothingFor(5.seconds),  // Wait before starting
      rampUsers(100).during(2.minutes),  // Ramp up to 100 users
      constantUsersPerSec(10).during(10.minutes),  // Maintain load
      rampUsersPerSec(10).to(50).during(5.minutes),  // Increase load
      constantUsersPerSec(50).during(15.minutes),  // Peak load
      rampUsersPerSec(50).to(0).during(2.minutes)  // Ramp down
    ).protocols(httpProtocol),
    
    purchasingScenario.inject(
      rampUsers(50).during(2.minutes),
      constantUsersPerSec(5).during(20.minutes)
    ).protocols(httpProtocol),
    
    adminScenario.inject(
      constantUsersPerSec(1).during(30.minutes)
    ).protocols(httpProtocol)
  ).assertions(
    // Global assertions
    global.responseTime.percentile3.lt(500),  // 95th percentile < 500ms
    global.failedRequests.percent.lt(1.0),    // Error rate < 1%
    global.successfulRequests.percent.gt(99),  // Success rate > 99%
    
    // Specific endpoint assertions
    details("Login API").responseTime.percentile3.lt(300),
    details("Checkout").responseTime.percentile3.lt(1000),
    details("Admin Statistics").responseTime.percentile3.lt(2000),
    
    // Throughput assertions
    forAll.requestsPerSec.gt(100),  // Overall throughput > 100 RPS
    
    // Response time distribution
    forAll.responseTime.mean.lt(200),
    forAll.responseTime.max.lt(5000)
  )
}

content.title: Performance Testing in CI/CD Pipelines
content.explanation:
Integrating performance tests into CI/CD transforms them from occasional exercises to continuous quality gates:

**Pipeline Stages**:
1. **Commit Stage**: Quick smoke tests (1-2 minutes)
2. **Acceptance Stage**: Baseline performance tests (5-10 minutes)
3. **Performance Stage**: Full load tests (30-60 minutes)
4. **Production Stage**: Canary testing with real traffic

**Implementation Strategies**:
• **Test Pyramid for Performance**:
  - Unit performance tests (microbenchmarks)
  - Component load tests (single service)
  - Integration load tests (full system)
• **Environment Strategy**:
  - Dedicated performance environment
  - Production-like data and configuration
  - Isolated from other testing
• **Data Management**:
  - Synthetic test data generation
  - Data refresh strategies
  - GDPR/compliance considerations

**Cost Optimization**:
• Run comprehensive tests only on release candidates
• Use spot instances for load generators
• Implement test data reuse strategies
• Monitor and optimize test duration

content.caption: GitLab CI/CD Pipeline with Performance Testing
content.code:
# .gitlab-ci.yml
stages:
  - build
  - test
  - performance
  - deploy
  - monitor

variables:
  PERFORMANCE_ENVIRONMENT: "performance-staging"
  K6_VERSION: "0.45.0"
  JMETER_VERSION: "5.5"

# Build stage
build:
  stage: build
  image: maven:3.8-openjdk-17
  script:
    - mvn clean compile
    - mvn package -DskipTests
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - target/*.jar
    expire_in: 1 week

# Unit and integration tests
unit-tests:
  stage: test
  image: maven:3.8-openjdk-17
  script:
    - mvn test
  artifacts:
    reports:
      junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
  coverage: '/Total.*?([0-9]{1,3})%/'  

api-tests:
  stage: test
  image: curlimages/curl:latest
  services:
    - name: postgres:14
      alias: database
    - name: redis:7
      alias: cache
  script:
    - ./scripts/wait-for-api.sh http://api:8080/health
    - ./scripts/run-api-tests.sh

# Performance tests
performance-smoke:
  stage: performance
  image: loadimpact/k6:$K6_VERSION
  variables:
    K6_CLOUD_TOKEN: $K6_CLOUD_TOKEN
  script:
    - echo "Running smoke performance test"
    - k6 run --out cloud scripts/performance/smoke-test.js
    - k6 cloud status --token $K6_CLOUD_TOKEN
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - k6-report.html
    expire_in: 1 week
  only:
    - merge_requests
    - main

performance-baseline:
  stage: performance
  image: loadimpact/k6:$K6_VERSION
  needs: ["performance-smoke"]
  script:
    - echo "Running baseline performance test"
    - k6 run --out cloud scripts/performance/baseline-test.js
    
    # Compare with previous baseline
    - ./scripts/compare-baseline.sh current-results.json baseline-results.json
    
    # Fail if performance degraded more than 10%
    - ./scripts/check-performance-gate.sh --threshold 10
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - performance-results/
      - comparison-report.html
    expire_in: 1 month
  only:
    - main
    - tags

performance-load:
  stage: performance
  image: justb4/jmeter:$JMETER_VERSION
  needs: ["performance-baseline"]
  parallel: 3  # Run tests in parallel
  script:
    - echo "Starting JMeter load test"
    - jmeter -n -t tests/performance/full-load.jmx
    - jmeter -g results.jtl -o report
    
    # Generate performance report
    - ./scripts/generate-performance-report.sh
    
    # Upload results to monitoring system
    - curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @summary.json $PERFORMANCE_MONITORING_URL
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - report/
      - results.jtl
      - summary.json
    reports:
      performance: summary.json
  only:
    - tags
  environment:
    name: $PERFORMANCE_ENVIRONMENT
    url: https://performance-api.example.com

# Performance gates
performance-gate:
  stage: performance
  image: alpine:latest
  needs: ["performance-baseline", "performance-load"]
  script:
    - echo "Checking performance gates"
    - apk add jq curl
    - ./scripts/check-performance-gates.sh
    
    # Example gate checks:
    - RESPONSE_TIME=$(cat summary.json | jq '.metrics."http_req_duration"."p(95)"')
    - if [ $(echo "$RESPONSE_TIME > 500" | bc) -eq 1 ]; then echo "Response time SLA violated: $RESPONSE_TIME ms" && exit 1; fi
    
    - ERROR_RATE=$(cat summary.json | jq '.metrics."http_req_failed".rate')
    - if [ $(echo "$ERROR_RATE > 0.01" | bc) -eq 1 ]; then echo "Error rate SLA violated: $ERROR_RATE" && exit 1; fi
  allow_failure: false

# Deployment stages
deploy-staging:
  stage: deploy
  script: ./scripts/deploy.sh staging
  environment:
    name: staging
    url: https://staging-api.example.com
  only:
    - main

canary-deploy:
  stage: deploy
  script: ./scripts/deploy-canary.sh
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://api.example.com
    deployment_tier: canary
  only:
    - tags

# Production monitoring
production-monitoring:
  stage: monitor
  image: curlimages/curl:latest
  script:
    - echo "Monitoring production performance"
    - ./scripts/monitor-production.sh
    
    # Compare production metrics with test results
    - ./scripts/compare-production-with-test.sh
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://api.example.com
  when: manual
  only:
    - tags

# Performance test on schedule
daily-performance-check:
  stage: performance
  image: loadimpact/k6:$K6_VERSION
  script:
    - k6 run scripts/performance/daily-check.js
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
      when: manual
  variables:
    TEST_TYPE: "daily"
  environment:
    name: $PERFORMANCE_ENVIRONMENT

content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Performance Test Automation Framework Integrates multiple tools, analyzes results, and generates reports """ import asyncio import json import statistics from dataclasses import dataclass from datetime import datetime from enum import Enum from typing import Dict, List, Optional import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import seaborn as sns from prometheus_api_client import PrometheusConnect from jinja2 import Template import requests class TestTool(Enum): JMETER = "jmeter" K6 = "k6" GATLING = "gatling" LOCUST = "locust" class TestType(Enum): LOAD = "load" STRESS = "stress" SPIKE = "spike" ENDURANCE = "endurance" SOAK = "soak" @dataclass class PerformanceMetrics: response_time_p50: float response_time_p95: float response_time_p99: float throughput: float # requests per second error_rate: float # percentage concurrent_users: int duration: int # seconds total_requests: int successful_requests: int failed_requests: int # Resource metrics cpu_utilization: Optional[float] = None memory_utilization: Optional[float] = None database_connections: Optional[int] = None @dataclass class SLARequirement: name: str metric: str condition: str # e.g., "< 500", "> 100", "< 0.01" severity: str # "critical", "warning", "info" class PerformanceTest: """ Base class for performance tests """ def __init__(self, name: str, tool: TestTool, test_type: TestType): self.name = name self.tool = tool self.test_type = test_type self.metrics: Optional[PerformanceMetrics] = None self.sla_requirements: List[SLARequirement] = [] self.test_results: Dict = {} def add_sla_requirement(self, sla: SLARequirement): self.sla_requirements.append(sla) async def execute(self): """Execute the performance test""" raise NotImplementedError async def collect_metrics(self): """Collect metrics from test execution""" raise NotImplementedError def validate_slas(self) -> Dict[str, bool]: """Validate test results against SLA requirements""" if not self.metrics: raise ValueError("No metrics collected. Run collect_metrics first.") results = {} for sla in self.sla_requirements: metric_value = getattr(self.metrics, sla.metric, None) if metric_value is None: results[sla.name] = False continue # Parse condition (simple implementation) if "<" in sla.condition: threshold = float(sla.condition.replace("<", "").strip()) results[sla.name] = metric_value < threshold elif ">" in sla.condition: threshold = float(sla.condition.replace(">", "").strip()) results[sla.name] = metric_value > threshold else: results[sla.name] = False return results def generate_report(self, output_path: str): """Generate HTML report""" sla_results = self.validate_slas() template_str = """ Performance Test Report - {{ test_name }}

Performance Test Report: {{ test_name }}

Tool: {{ tool }}

Type: {{ test_type }}

Date: {{ date }}

Duration: {{ metrics.duration }} seconds

Concurrent Users: {{ metrics.concurrent_users }}

Key Metrics

95th Percentile Response Time
{{ metrics.response_time_p95 }} ms
Throughput
{{ metrics.throughput }} req/s
Error Rate
{{ (metrics.error_rate * 100)|round(2) }}%
Total Requests
{{ metrics.total_requests }}

SLA Validation

{% for sla in sla_requirements %} {% set result = sla_results[sla.name] %} {% endfor %}
SLA Requirement Condition Actual Value Status
{{ sla.name }} {{ sla.metric }} {{ sla.condition }} {{ getattr(metrics, sla.metric, 'N/A') }} {{ 'PASS' if result else 'FAIL' }}

Recommendations

    {% for recommendation in recommendations %}
  • {{ recommendation }}
    • {% endfor %}
""" template = Template(template_str) recommendations = self._generate_recommendations() html_content = template.render( test_name=self.name, tool=self.tool.value, test_type=self.test_type.value, date=datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), metrics=self.metrics, sla_requirements=self.sla_requirements, sla_results=sla_results, recommendations=recommendations ) with open(output_path, 'w') as f: f.write(html_content) def _generate_recommendations(self) -> List[str]: """Generate recommendations based on test results""" recommendations = [] if not self.metrics: return recommendations # Example recommendations based on thresholds if self.metrics.response_time_p95 > 500: recommendations.append( "95th percentile response time exceeds 500ms. Consider optimizing database queries or adding caching." ) if self.metrics.error_rate > 0.01: recommendations.append( f"Error rate {self.metrics.error_rate*100:.2f}% exceeds 1%. Investigate server logs for failures." ) if self.metrics.cpu_utilization and self.metrics.cpu_utilization > 80: recommendations.append( f"CPU utilization {self.metrics.cpu_utilization:.1f}% is high. Consider scaling horizontally." ) return recommendations class JMeterTest(PerformanceTest): """ JMeter-specific test implementation """ def __init__(self, name: str, jmx_path: str): super().__init__(name, TestTool.JMETER, TestType.LOAD) self.jmx_path = jmx_path self.results_file = "results.jtl" async def execute(self): """Execute JMeter test""" import subprocess cmd = [ "jmeter", "-n", "-t", self.jmx_path, "-l", self.results_file, "-e", "-o", "report" ] process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec( *cmd, stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE ) stdout, stderr = await process.communicate() if process.returncode != 0: raise RuntimeError(f"JMeter test failed: {stderr.decode()}") self.test_results["output"] = stdout.decode() async def collect_metrics(self): """Collect metrics from JMeter results""" import pandas as pd # Parse JTL file df = pd.read_csv(self.results_file) # Calculate metrics response_times = df["elapsed"].tolist() self.metrics = PerformanceMetrics( response_time_p50=statistics.median(response_times), response_time_p95=pd.Series(response_times).quantile(0.95), response_time_p99=pd.Series(response_times).quantile(0.99), throughput=len(df) / (df["timeStamp"].max() - df["timeStamp"].min()) * 1000, error_rate=df["success"].value_counts(normalize=True).get(False, 0), concurrent_users=df["threadName"].nunique(), duration=(df["timeStamp"].max() - df["timeStamp"].min()) / 1000, total_requests=len(df), successful_requests=df["success"].sum(), failed_requests=(~df["success"]).sum() ) class K6Test(PerformanceTest): """ k6-specific test implementation """ def __init__(self, name: str, script_path: str): super().__init__(name, TestTool.K6, TestType.LOAD) self.script_path = script_path self.results_file = "results.json" async def execute(self): """Execute k6 test""" import subprocess cmd = ["k6", "run", "--out", f"json={self.results_file}", self.script_path] process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec( *cmd, stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE ) stdout, stderr = await process.communicate() if process.returncode != 0: raise RuntimeError(f"k6 test failed: {stderr.decode()}") self.test_results["output"] = stdout.decode() async def collect_metrics(self): """Collect metrics from k6 results""" with open(self.results_file) as f: data = json.load(f) metrics = data["metrics"] self.metrics = PerformanceMetrics( response_time_p50=metrics["http_req_duration"]["values"]["med"], response_time_p95=metrics["http_req_duration"]["values"]["p(95)"], response_time_p99=metrics["http_req_duration"]["values"]["p(99)"], throughput=metrics["http_reqs"]["values"]["rate"], error_rate=metrics["http_req_failed"]["values"]["rate"], concurrent_users=metrics["vus"]["values"]["max"], duration=metrics["iteration_duration"]["values"]["max"] / 1000, total_requests=metrics["http_reqs"]["values"]["count"], successful_requests=int(metrics["http_reqs"]["values"]["count"] * (1 - metrics["http_req_failed"]["values"]["rate"])), failed_requests=int(metrics["http_reqs"]["values"]["count"] * metrics["http_req_failed"]["values"]["rate"]) ) class PerformanceTestOrchestrator: """ Orchestrates multiple performance tests and generates consolidated reports """ def __init__(self): self.tests: List[PerformanceTest] = [] self.prometheus = PrometheusConnect(url="http://prometheus:9090") def add_test(self, test: PerformanceTest): self.tests.append(test) async def run_all_tests(self): """Run all registered tests""" tasks = [test.execute() for test in self.tests] await asyncio.gather(*tasks) # Collect metrics for all tests for test in self.tests: await test.collect_metrics() def generate_consolidated_report(self, output_path: str): """Generate consolidated report for all tests""" # Create comparison charts self._create_comparison_charts() # Generate summary report summary_data = [] for test in self.tests: if test.metrics: summary_data.append({ "Test Name": test.name, "Tool": test.tool.value, "p95 Response Time (ms)": test.metrics.response_time_p95, "Throughput (req/s)": test.metrics.throughput, "Error Rate (%)": test.metrics.error_rate * 100, "Concurrent Users": test.metrics.concurrent_users }) df = pd.DataFrame(summary_data) # Create HTML report report_html = """ Consolidated Performance Test Report

Performance Test Comparison

{{ df.to_html() }}

Response Time Comparison

Throughput Comparison

""" with open(output_path, 'w') as f: f.write(report_html) def _create_comparison_charts(self): """Create comparison charts for all tests""" test_names = [] p95_times = [] throughputs = [] for test in self.tests: if test.metrics: test_names.append(test.name) p95_times.append(test.metrics.response_time_p95) throughputs.append(test.metrics.throughput) # Response times chart plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6)) plt.bar(test_names, p95_times) plt.title('95th Percentile Response Time Comparison') plt.xlabel('Test') plt.ylabel('Response Time (ms)') plt.axhline(y=500, color='r', linestyle='--', label='SLA (500ms)') plt.legend() plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig('response_times.png') plt.close() # Throughput chart plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6)) plt.bar(test_names, throughputs) plt.title('Throughput Comparison') plt.xlabel('Test') plt.ylabel('Requests per Second') plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig('throughput.png') plt.close() # Example usage async def main(): """Example usage of the performance testing framework""" # Create JMeter test jmeter_test = JMeterTest( name="E-Commerce API Load Test", jmx_path="tests/ecommerce-load.jmx" ) jmeter_test.add_sla_requirement(SLARequirement( name="Response Time SLA", metric="response_time_p95", condition="< 500", severity="critical" )) jmeter_test.add_sla_requirement(SLARequirement( name="Error Rate SLA", metric="error_rate", condition="< 0.01", severity="critical" )) # Create k6 test k6_test = K6Test( name="User Authentication Stress Test", script_path="tests/auth-stress.js" ) k6_test.add_sla_requirement(SLARequirement( name="Auth Response Time", metric="response_time_p95", condition="< 300", severity="critical" )) # Create orchestrator orchestrator = PerformanceTestOrchestrator() orchestrator.add_test(jmeter_test) orchestrator.add_test(k6_test) # Run tests print("Running performance tests...") await orchestrator.run_all_tests() # Generate reports print("Generating reports...") jmeter_test.generate_report("reports/jmeter-report.html") k6_test.generate_report("reports/k6-report.html") orchestrator.generate_consolidated_report("reports/consolidated-report.html") # Check SLAs print("\nSLA Validation Results:") for test in [jmeter_test, k6_test]: print(f"\n{test.name}:") sla_results = test.validate_slas() for sla_name, passed in sla_results.items(): status = "PASS" if passed else "FAIL" print(f" {sla_name}: {status}") if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

content.title: Advanced Analysis Techniques
content.explanation:
**Statistical Analysis for Performance Testing**:

**Confidence Intervals**:
Performance test results are samples, not absolute truths. Use confidence intervals:
```python
import scipy.stats as stats
import numpy as np

response_times = [150, 155, 160, 145, 170, ...]
confidence_level = 0.95
n = len(response_times)
mean = np.mean(response_times)
std_err = stats.sem(response_times)
ci = stats.t.interval(confidence_level, n-1, loc=mean, scale=std_err)
# Result: (148.2, 161.8) - 95% confident true mean is between these values
```

**Trend Analysis**:
Identify performance degradation over time:
```python
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import pandas as pd

# Load historical results
df = pd.read_csv('historical_performance.csv')
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
df['day_num'] = (df['date'] - df['date'].min()).dt.days

# Fit trend line
X = df[['day_num']]
y = df['response_time_p95']
model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
trend_slope = model.coef_[0]
# Positive slope means performance is degrading
```

**Anomaly Detection**:
Identify unusual patterns in performance metrics:
```python
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest

# Train on normal performance data
clf = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1)
clf.fit(normal_performance_data)

# Predict anomalies
anomalies = clf.predict(test_performance_data)
# -1 indicates anomaly
```

**Root Cause Analysis**:
Correlate application metrics with infrastructure metrics:
```python
# Correlate response time with database connections
correlation = df['response_time_p95'].corr(df['db_connections'])
if correlation > 0.8:
    print("High correlation: Database connections affect response time")
```

**Capacity Planning**:
Use Little's Law for capacity estimation:
```python
# Little's Law: L = λW
# L = average number of requests in system
# λ = arrival rate (requests/second)
# W = average time in system (seconds)

arrival_rate = 100  # requests/second
average_response_time = 0.2  # seconds
requests_in_system = arrival_rate * average_response_time  # = 20

# If system can handle 50 concurrent requests
max_arrival_rate = 50 / average_response_time  # = 250 requests/second
```

items.myth: Performance testing is only about finding the maximum load
items.reality: It's about understanding behavior across the entire load spectrum, establishing baselines, and ensuring reliability

items.myth: If it works for 100 users, it will work for 1000
items.reality: Systems don't scale linearly. Bottlenecks appear at specific thresholds due to resource contention, locking, or architectural limits

items.myth: Production is the best place to performance test
items.reality: Testing in production can cause outages and affect real users. Use production-like environments with synthetic load

items.myth: Performance tests should run as fast as possible
items.reality: Real users have think times. Tests without realistic pacing can overwhelm systems in unrealistic ways

items.myth: Once performance is optimized, no need to re-test
items.reality: Performance degrades over time due to code changes, data growth, and infrastructure changes

content.title: Why API Security Testing is Non-Negotiable
content.explanation:
APIs are the backbone of modern applications, making them prime targets for attackers. Unlike traditional web applications where security was often perimeter-based, APIs expose business logic directly. A single vulnerable API can lead to:

**Business Impact**:
• **Data breaches**: Customer PII, payment information, intellectual property
• **Financial loss**: Fraudulent transactions, regulatory fines (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA)
• **Reputation damage**: Loss of customer trust, brand devaluation
• **Service disruption**: DDoS attacks, ransomware, service unavailability

**The API Attack Surface**:
1. **Authentication endpoints**: Credential stuffing, brute force attacks
2. **Business logic endpoints**: Parameter manipulation, privilege escalation
3. **Data endpoints**: SQL injection, NoSQL injection, data exfiltration
4. **File endpoints**: Path traversal, file upload vulnerabilities
5. **Configuration endpoints**: Information disclosure, misconfigurations

**Shift-Left Security**:
Security testing must be integrated into the development lifecycle, not an afterthought. Automated API security tests should run alongside functional tests in CI/CD pipelines.

content.title: Security Testing Methodology
content.explanation:
Effective API security testing follows a structured approach:

**1. Discovery Phase**:
• **API Inventory**: Catalog all endpoints, methods, parameters
• **Documentation Review**: Analyze OpenAPI/Swagger specifications
• **Traffic Analysis**: Monitor real traffic to find undocumented endpoints

**2. Authentication & Authorization Testing**:
• **Authentication bypass**: Test without tokens, expired tokens, malformed tokens
• **Authorization testing**: Horizontal/vertical privilege escalation
• **Session management**: Token lifetime, revocation, replay attacks

**3. Input Validation Testing**:
• **Injection attacks**: SQL, NoSQL, LDAP, OS command, XML, GraphQL
• **Business logic validation**: Boundary testing, negative testing
• **Data type validation**: Type confusion, overflow/underflow

**4. Configuration & Deployment Testing**:
• **Information disclosure**: Error messages, stack traces, headers
• **Cryptographic issues**: Weak algorithms, improper TLS configuration
• **CORS misconfiguration**: Overly permissive cross-origin policies

**5. Business Logic Testing**:
• **Workflow bypass**: Skipping steps, changing order
• **Race conditions**: Concurrent requests causing inconsistent state
• **Financial logic**: Negative prices, duplicate transactions

**6. Advanced Persistent Testing**:
• **Fuzzing**: Automated input generation to find edge cases
• **Dependency scanning**: Known vulnerabilities in libraries
• **Compliance testing**: GDPR, PCI-DSS, HIPAA requirements

content.title: Authentication Bypass Techniques
content.explanation:
Authentication is the gatekeeper of API security. Testing must validate all possible bypass scenarios:

**Token Manipulation Attacks**:
• **JWT Attacks**:
  - Algorithm confusion (changing 'alg' to 'none')
  - Weak secret brute forcing
  - Expired token acceptance
  - Signature stripping
• **OAuth/OIDC Flaws**:
  - Authorization code interception
  - Redirect URI manipulation
  - State parameter validation bypass
  - Token replay attacks

**Credential Attacks**:
• **Brute Force**: Unlimited login attempts
• **Credential Stuffing**: Reused credentials from breaches
• **Password Spraying**: Few passwords across many accounts
• **Account Enumeration**: Different responses for valid/invalid users

**Session Management Flaws**:
• **Session Fixation**: Attacker sets session ID for victim
• **Session Hijacking**: Stealing session tokens via XSS
• **Insecure Token Storage**: Tokens in localStorage, cookies without flags
• **Missing Token Revocation**: Tokens remain valid after logout/password change

**Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass**:
• **Code Brute Forcing**: Limited MFA code attempts
• **Time-based attacks**: OTP code reuse windows
• **Recovery flow bypass**: Password reset without MFA
• **SMS/Email interception**: SIM swapping, email forwarding

content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
API Authentication Security Testing Framework
Tests various authentication bypass and token manipulation attacks
"""

import requests
import jwt
import json
import time
import hashlib
import hmac
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

class AuthMethod(Enum):
    JWT = "jwt"
    OAUTH2 = "oauth2"
    API_KEY = "api_key"
    BASIC_AUTH = "basic_auth"
    CUSTOM = "custom"

class TestResult(Enum):
    PASS = "pass"
    FAIL = "fail"
    WARNING = "warning"
    ERROR = "error"

@dataclass
class SecurityTest:
    name: str
    description: str
    severity: str  # critical, high, medium, low
    test_function: callable
    expected_result: TestResult

class APIAuthSecurityTester:
    """
    Comprehensive API authentication security testing framework
    """
    
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, auth_method: AuthMethod):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip('/')
        self.auth_method = auth_method
        self.session = requests.Session()
        self.session.headers.update({
            'User-Agent': 'APISecurityTester/1.0',
            'Accept': 'application/json'
        })
        self.test_results = []
        self.valid_tokens = []
        
    def add_test_result(self, test_name: str, result: TestResult, 
                       details: str, severity: str):
        """Record test result"""
        self.test_results.append({
            'test': test_name,
            'result': result,
            'details': details,
            'severity': severity,
            'timestamp': time.time()
        })
    
    def test_jwt_none_algorithm(self) -> TestResult:
        """Test JWT 'none' algorithm vulnerability"""
        test_name = "JWT Algorithm None Attack"
        try:
            # Create a token with 'none' algorithm
            payload = {
                'sub': 'admin',
                'iat': int(time.time()),
                'exp': int(time.time()) + 3600
            }
            
            # Try different none algorithm variations
            none_tokens = [
                jwt.encode(payload, '', algorithm='none'),
                jwt.encode(payload, None, algorithm='none'),
                # Some libraries use 'alg': 'none' in header
                jwt.encode(payload, '', algorithm='HS256').rsplit('.', 1)[0] + '.',
            ]
            
            for token in none_tokens:
                self.session.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {token}'
                response = self.session.get(f'{self.base_url}/api/user/profile')
                
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                        f'Accepted none-algorithm token: {token}',
                                        'critical')
                    return TestResult.FAIL
            
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                'Rejected none-algorithm tokens', 'medium')
            return TestResult.PASS
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_jwt_weak_secret_bruteforce(self, common_secrets: List[str]) -> TestResult:
        """Test weak JWT secrets using common password list"""
        test_name = "JWT Weak Secret Brute Force"
        try:
            # Get a valid JWT token to analyze
            login_response = self.session.post(
                f'{self.base_url}/api/auth/login',
                json={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'}
            )
            
            if login_response.status_code != 200:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    'Could not obtain test token', 'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
            
            token = login_response.json().get('token')
            if not token:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    'No token in response', 'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
            
            # Try to decode with common secrets
            for secret in common_secrets:
                try:
                    decoded = jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=['HS256'])
                    self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                        f'Weak secret found: {secret}',
                                        'high')
                    return TestResult.FAIL
                except jwt.InvalidSignatureError:
                    continue
                except Exception:
                    continue
            
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                'No weak secrets found', 'medium')
            return TestResult.PASS
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_expired_token_acceptance(self, valid_token: str) -> TestResult:
        """Test if expired tokens are still accepted"""
        test_name = "Expired Token Acceptance"
        try:
            # Create an expired token
            payload = {
                'sub': 'testuser',
                'iat': int(time.time()) - 7200,  # 2 hours ago
                'exp': int(time.time()) - 3600   # Expired 1 hour ago
            }
            
            # Need to sign it properly - this requires knowing the secret
            # For demonstration, we'll modify a valid token's timestamp
            try:
                decoded = jwt.decode(valid_token, options={'verify_signature': False})
                decoded['exp'] = int(time.time()) - 3600  # Set to expired
                
                # Try to re-encode - this won't work without secret
                # In real test, you'd need the signing key
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    'Expired token test requires signing key',
                                    'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
                
            except Exception as e:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                    f'Token manipulation failed: {str(e)}', 'low')
                return TestResult.ERROR
                
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_brute_force_protection(self, endpoint: str, 
                                   username: str, passwords: List[str]) -> TestResult:
        """Test login endpoint brute force protection"""
        test_name = "Brute Force Protection"
        failed_attempts = 0
        lockout_triggered = False
        
        try:
            for i, password in enumerate(passwords[:20]):  # Limit to 20 attempts
                response = self.session.post(
                    f'{self.base_url}{endpoint}',
                    json={'username': username, 'password': password},
                    timeout=5
                )
                
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                        f'Successful login with password {password} on attempt {i+1}',
                                        'critical')
                    return TestResult.FAIL
                elif response.status_code == 429:  # Too Many Requests
                    lockout_triggered = True
                    break
                elif response.status_code == 401:
                    failed_attempts += 1
                
                # Small delay between attempts
                time.sleep(0.1)
            
            if lockout_triggered:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                    f'Rate limiting triggered after {failed_attempts} attempts',
                                    'medium')
                return TestResult.PASS
            else:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                    f'No rate limiting after {failed_attempts} failed attempts',
                                    'high')
                return TestResult.FAIL
                
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_account_enumeration(self, endpoint: str) -> TestResult:
        """Test for username enumeration vulnerability"""
        test_name = "Account Enumeration"
        
        # Common usernames to test
        test_usernames = [
            'admin', 'administrator', 'root', 'test', 'user',
            'admin@example.com', 'user@example.com'
        ]
        
        responses = {}
        
        try:
            for username in test_usernames:
                response = self.session.post(
                    f'{self.base_url}{endpoint}',
                    json={'username': username, 'password': 'wrongpassword'},
                    timeout=5
                )
                
                responses[username] = {
                    'status': response.status_code,
                    'time': response.elapsed.total_seconds(),
                    'body': response.text,
                    'headers': dict(response.headers)
                }
                
                time.sleep(0.2)  # Avoid rate limiting
            
            # Analyze responses for differences that could indicate valid users
            status_codes = [r['status'] for r in responses.values()]
            response_times = [r['time'] for r in responses.values()]
            
            # Check if any responses are different
            if len(set(status_codes)) > 1:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                    f'Different status codes indicate username enumeration: {set(status_codes)}',
                                    'medium')
                return TestResult.FAIL
            
            # Check response time differences (timing attack)
            avg_time = sum(response_times) / len(response_times)
            significant_differences = [
                t for t in response_times 
                if abs(t - avg_time) > avg_time * 0.5  # 50% difference
            ]
            
            if significant_differences:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                    'Significant response time differences indicate timing attack vulnerability',
                                    'medium')
                return TestResult.FAIL
            
            # Check response body differences
            bodies = [r['body'] for r in responses.values()]
            if len(set(bodies)) > 1:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                    'Different response bodies indicate username enumeration',
                                    'medium')
                return TestResult.FAIL
            
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                'No username enumeration detected', 'low')
            return TestResult.PASS
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_horizontal_privilege_escalation(self, user1_token: str, 
                                           user2_token: str, 
                                           resource_endpoint: str) -> TestResult:
        """Test if User A can access User B's resources"""
        test_name = "Horizontal Privilege Escalation"
        
        try:
            # First, get User 1's resource ID
            self.session.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {user1_token}'
            user1_response = self.session.get(f'{self.base_url}{resource_endpoint}')
            
            if user1_response.status_code != 200:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    f'Cannot access User 1 resources: {user1_response.status_code}',
                                    'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
            
            # Extract a resource ID from User 1's response
            resources = user1_response.json()
            if not resources:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    'No resources found for User 1', 'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
            
            resource_id = resources[0].get('id')
            if not resource_id:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    'No resource ID found', 'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
            
            # Now try to access User 1's resource as User 2
            self.session.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {user2_token}'
            user2_response = self.session.get(
                f'{self.base_url}{resource_endpoint}/{resource_id}'
            )
            
            if user2_response.status_code == 200:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                    f'User 2 accessed User 1\'s resource {resource_id}',
                                    'critical')
                return TestResult.FAIL
            elif user2_response.status_code == 403:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                    'Proper authorization check in place', 'medium')
                return TestResult.PASS
            else:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    f'Unexpected status code: {user2_response.status_code}',
                                    'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
                
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_vertical_privilege_escalation(self, user_token: str, 
                                         admin_endpoint: str) -> TestResult:
        """Test if regular user can access admin endpoints"""
        test_name = "Vertical Privilege Escalation"
        
        try:
            self.session.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {user_token}'
            response = self.session.get(f'{self.base_url}{admin_endpoint}')
            
            if response.status_code == 200:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                    f'Regular user accessed admin endpoint: {admin_endpoint}',
                                    'critical')
                return TestResult.FAIL
            elif response.status_code == 403:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                    'Admin endpoint properly protected', 'medium')
                return TestResult.PASS
            else:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    f'Unexpected status code: {response.status_code}',
                                    'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
                
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_mass_assignment(self, create_endpoint: str, token: str, 
                           extra_fields: Dict) -> TestResult:
        """Test for mass assignment vulnerability"""
        test_name = "Mass Assignment"
        
        try:
            self.session.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {token}'
            
            # Normal payload
            normal_payload = {
                'name': 'Test Item',
                'description': 'Test description'
            }
            
            # Payload with extra fields that shouldn't be settable by user
            malicious_payload = {**normal_payload, **extra_fields}
            
            response = self.session.post(
                f'{self.base_url}{create_endpoint}',
                json=malicious_payload
            )
            
            if response.status_code == 201 or response.status_code == 200:
                # Check if extra fields were accepted
                created_resource = response.json()
                
                accepted_extra_fields = []
                for field in extra_fields:
                    if field in created_resource:
                        accepted_extra_fields.append(field)
                
                if accepted_extra_fields:
                    self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                        f'Mass assignment vulnerability: fields {accepted_extra_fields} accepted',
                                        'high')
                    return TestResult.FAIL
                else:
                    self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                        'Extra fields ignored', 'medium')
                    return TestResult.PASS
            else:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.WARNING,
                                    f'Request failed: {response.status_code}',
                                    'low')
                return TestResult.WARNING
                
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def test_rate_limiting(self, endpoint: str, token: str, 
                         requests_per_minute: int = 100) -> TestResult:
        """Test rate limiting implementation"""
        test_name = "Rate Limiting"
        
        try:
            self.session.headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {token}'
            
            successful_requests = 0
            limited_requests = 0
            start_time = time.time()
            
            # Make rapid requests
            for i in range(requests_per_minute):
                response = self.session.get(f'{self.base_url}{endpoint}')
                
                if response.status_code == 200:
                    successful_requests += 1
                elif response.status_code == 429:  # Too Many Requests
                    limited_requests += 1
                    break
                
                # Small delay to avoid overwhelming
                time.sleep(0.01)
            
            elapsed = time.time() - start_time
            requests_per_second = successful_requests / elapsed if elapsed > 0 else 0
            
            if limited_requests > 0:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.PASS,
                                    f'Rate limiting triggered after {successful_requests} requests ({requests_per_second:.1f} req/sec)',
                                    'medium')
                return TestResult.PASS
            else:
                self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.FAIL,
                                    f'No rate limiting after {successful_requests} requests ({requests_per_second:.1f} req/sec)',
                                    'high')
                return TestResult.FAIL
                
        except Exception as e:
            self.add_test_result(test_name, TestResult.ERROR,
                                f'Test error: {str(e)}', 'low')
            return TestResult.ERROR
    
    def run_all_tests(self) -> Dict:
        """Run all security tests"""
        print(f"Running API security tests for {self.base_url}")
        print(f"Authentication method: {self.auth_method.value}")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        # Run tests based on authentication method
        if self.auth_method == AuthMethod.JWT:
            self.test_jwt_none_algorithm()
            
            common_secrets = ['secret', 'password', '123456', 'admin', 'token', 'key']
            self.test_jwt_weak_secret_bruteforce(common_secrets)
        
        # Common tests for all authentication methods
        self.test_brute_force_protection(
            '/api/auth/login',
            'testuser',
            ['password', '123456', 'admin', 'test', 'pass']
        )
        
        self.test_account_enumeration('/api/auth/login')
        
        # Generate report
        critical_fails = [r for r in self.test_results 
                         if r['result'] == TestResult.FAIL and r['severity'] == 'critical']
        high_fails = [r for r in self.test_results 
                     if r['result'] == TestResult.FAIL and r['severity'] == 'high']
        
        report = {
            'summary': {
                'total_tests': len(self.test_results),
                'passed': len([r for r in self.test_results if r['result'] == TestResult.PASS]),
                'failed': len([r for r in self.test_results if r['result'] == TestResult.FAIL]),
                'warnings': len([r for r in self.test_results if r['result'] == TestResult.WARNING]),
                'errors': len([r for r in self.test_results if r['result'] == TestResult.ERROR]),
                'critical_vulnerabilities': len(critical_fails),
                'high_vulnerabilities': len(high_fails)
            },
            'results': self.test_results,
            'recommendations': self.generate_recommendations()
        }
        
        return report
    
    def generate_recommendations(self) -> List[str]:
        """Generate security recommendations based on test results"""
        recommendations = []
        
        for result in self.test_results:
            if result['result'] == TestResult.FAIL:
                if 'JWT Algorithm None' in result['test']:
                    recommendations.append(
                        "Reject JWT tokens with 'none' algorithm. Validate token algorithm before processing."
                    )
                elif 'Weak Secret' in result['test']:
                    recommendations.append(
                        "Use strong, random secrets for JWT signing. Rotate secrets regularly."
                    )
                elif 'Brute Force' in result['test']:
                    recommendations.append(
                        "Implement rate limiting on login endpoints. Use account lockout after multiple failures."
                    )
                elif 'Account Enumeration' in result['test']:
                    recommendations.append(
                        "Standardize error responses for valid/invalid credentials to prevent username enumeration."
                    )
                
        # General recommendations
        recommendations.extend([
            "Implement proper input validation and sanitization",
            "Use HTTPS for all API communications",
            "Implement proper CORS policies",
            "Regularly rotate secrets and keys",
            "Monitor and log authentication attempts",
            "Implement multi-factor authentication for sensitive operations"
        ])
        
        return list(set(recommendations))  # Remove duplicates

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Initialize tester
    tester = APIAuthSecurityTester(
        base_url="https://api.example.com",
        auth_method=AuthMethod.JWT
    )
    
    # Run tests
    report = tester.run_all_tests()
    
    # Print summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("SECURITY TEST SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 60)
    summary = report['summary']
    print(f"Total Tests: {summary['total_tests']}")
    print(f"Passed: {summary['passed']}")
    print(f"Failed: {summary['failed']}")
    print(f"Critical Vulnerabilities: {summary['critical_vulnerabilities']}")
    print(f"High Vulnerabilities: {summary['high_vulnerabilities']}")
    
    # Print failed tests
    if summary['failed'] > 0:
        print("\nFAILED TESTS:")
        for result in report['results']:
            if result['result'] == TestResult.FAIL:
                print(f"  [{result['severity'].upper()}] {result['test']}")
                print(f"      Details: {result['details']}")
    
    # Print recommendations
    if report['recommendations']:
        print("\nRECOMMENDATIONS:")
        for i, rec in enumerate(report['recommendations'][:10], 1):
            print(f"  {i}. {rec}")
    
    # Save report to file
    with open('security_test_report.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(report, f, indent=2, default=str)
    
    print("\nDetailed report saved to: security_test_report.json")

content.title: Comprehensive Injection Testing
content.explanation:
Injection attacks remain the most critical API vulnerabilities. Modern APIs face multiple injection vectors:

**SQL Injection Evolution**:
• **Classic SQLi**: UNION-based, error-based, blind SQLi
• **Modern SQLi**: Time-based, out-of-band (DNS exfiltration)
• **ORM Injection**: Bypassing ORM sanitization
• **NoSQL Injection**: MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis specific payloads

**NoSQL Injection Techniques**:
```javascript
// MongoDB Injection Examples
{"$where": "sleep(5000)"}  // Time-based
{"$ne": ""}  // Not equal to empty (bypass authentication)
{"$regex": ".*"}  // Regex injection
{"$function": "function() { return sleep(5000) }"}  // Function injection
```

**Command Injection Vectors**:
• **System commands**: Through file uploads, webhooks, web sockets
• **Template injection**: Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker template engines
• **Expression Language Injection**: SpEL (Spring), OGNL, MVEL
• **XPath Injection**: XML parsing endpoints

**GraphQL Injection**:
• **Query depth attacks**: Deeply nested queries causing DoS
• **Field name injection**: Malicious field names in introspection
• **Directive injection**: Malicious GraphQL directives

**API Parameter Pollution**:
• **HTTP Parameter Pollution**: Multiple parameters with same name
• **JSON/XML Property Pollution**: Duplicate keys with different values
• **Type Confusion**: Sending string where number expected

**File Upload Vulnerabilities**:
• **Malicious file types**: .php, .jsp, .exe disguised as images
• **Zip bombs**: Compressed files that explode to huge size
• **Path traversal**: ../../etc/passwd in filename
• **Malicious metadata**: EXIF data, PDF JavaScript
