content.code:
# docker-compose.yml - Pact Broker with PostgreSQL
version: '3.8'

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: pactbroker
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: pactbroker
      POSTGRES_DB: pactbroker
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U pactbroker"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  pact-broker:
    image: pactfoundation/pact-broker:2.107.0
    ports:
      - "9292:9292"
    environment:
      PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_USERNAME: pactbroker
      PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_PASSWORD: pactbroker
      PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_HOST: postgres
      PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_NAME: pactbroker
      PACT_BROKER_WEBHOOK_SCHEME_WHITELIST: "http https"
      PACT_BROKER_LOG_LEVEL: INFO
      PACT_BROKER_BASE_URL: "http://localhost:9292"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  postgres-data:

# .github/workflows/pact-consumer.yml - Consumer CI/CD
name: Consumer Pact Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  pact-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    services:
      pact-broker:
        image: pactfoundation/pact-broker:2.107.0
        env:
          PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_ADAPTER: sqlite
          PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_NAME: pact_broker.sqlite
        ports:
          - 9292:9292
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Set up Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: '17'
        distribution: 'temurin'
    
    - name: Run consumer pact tests
      run: |
        ./gradlew test --tests "*ConsumerTest"
      env:
        PACT_BROKER_URL: http://localhost:9292
    
    - name: Publish pact to broker
      if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      run: |
        ./gradlew pactPublish
      env:
        PACT_BROKER_BASE_URL: http://localhost:9292
        PACT_BROKER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PACT_BROKER_TOKEN }}
        
    - name: Check if we can deploy (consumer)
      if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      run: |
        ./gradlew pactCanIDeploy \
          -Ppact.provider.version=1.2.0 \
          -Ppactbroker.consumerversionselectors.rawjson='[{\"latest\": true}]'

# .github/workflows/pact-provider.yml - Provider CI/CD
name: Provider Pact Verification

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # Trigger when pact changes in broker
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [pact_changed]

jobs:
  pact-verification:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    services:
      pact-broker:
        image: pactfoundation/pact-broker:2.107.0
        env:
          PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_ADAPTER: sqlite
          PACT_BROKER_DATABASE_NAME: pact_broker.sqlite
        ports:
          - 9292:9292
      
      product-service:
        image: product-service:test
        ports:
          - 8080:8080
        env:
          SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE: test
          DATABASE_URL: jdbc:h2:mem:testdb
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Set up Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: '17'
        distribution: 'temurin'
    
    - name: Wait for service to be ready
      run: |
        timeout 60 bash -c 'until curl -s http://localhost:8080/health > /dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
    
    - name: Run provider pact verification
      run: |
        ./gradlew pactVerify \
          -Ppact.provider.version=${GITHUB_SHA:0:7} \
          -Ppact.provider.tag=main \
          -Ppact.verifier.publishResults=true
      env:
        PACT_BROKER_BASE_URL: http://localhost:9292
        PACT_BROKER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PACT_BROKER_TOKEN }}
    
    - name: Check if we can deploy (provider)
      if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      run: |
        ./gradlew pactCanIDeploy \
          -Ppact.provider.version=${GITHUB_SHA:0:7} \
          -Ppactbroker.providerversionselectors.rawjson='[{\"latest\": true}]'

# Jenkins Pipeline Script
pipeline {
    agent any
    
    environment {
        PACT_BROKER_URL = 'https://pact-broker.example.com'
        PACT_BROKER_TOKEN = credentials('pact-broker-token')
    }
    
    stages {
        stage('Build') {
            steps {
                sh './gradlew build'
            }
        }
        
        stage('Consumer Pact Tests') {
            when {
                expression { return env.JOB_NAME.contains('consumer') }
            }
            steps {
                sh './gradlew test --tests "*ConsumerTest"'
            }
            post {
                success {
                    sh '''
                        ./gradlew pactPublish \
                          -Ppact.provider.version=${GIT_COMMIT} \
                          -Ppactbroker.consumerversionselectors.rawjson='[{"latest": true}]'
                    '''
                }
            }
        }
        
        stage('Provider Pact Verification') {
            when {
                expression { return env.JOB_NAME.contains('provider') }
            }
            steps {
                // Start provider service
                sh 'docker-compose up -d product-service'
                
                // Wait for service
                sh 'sleep 30'
                
                // Run verification
                sh '''
                    ./gradlew pactVerify \
                      -Ppact.provider.version=${GIT_COMMIT} \
                      -Ppact.provider.tag=${BRANCH_NAME} \
                      -Ppact.verifier.publishResults=true
                '''
            }
        }
        
        stage('Can I Deploy?') {
            steps {
                script {
                    def canDeploy = sh(
                        script: '''
                            ./gradlew pactCanIDeploy \
                              -Ppact.provider.version=${GIT_COMMIT} \
                              -Ppactbroker.providerversionselectors.rawjson='[{"latest": true}]' \
                              -q --console=plain
                        ''',
                        returnStdout: true
                    ).trim()
                    
                    if (canDeploy.contains('Computer says no')) {
                        error('Cannot deploy - pact verification failed')
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

content.title: Advanced Pact Patterns
Contract Testing at Scale
content.explanation:
Implementing contract testing across dozens or hundreds of microservices requires careful planning:

**Organizational Challenges**:
• **Team coordination**: Who owns which contracts?
• **Change management**: How are breaking changes communicated?
• **Versioning strategy**: Semantic versioning for APIs
• **Onboarding**: Training teams on contract testing

**Technical Architecture**:
1. **Centralized Pact Broker**: Single source of truth for all contracts
2. **Self-Service Portal**: Teams can view contracts, verification status
3. **Automated Verification**: CI/CD triggers verification on pact changes
4. **Monitoring & Alerting**: Track contract compliance metrics

**Versioning Strategy**:
• **Semantic Versioning**: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH for APIs
• **Consumer Version Selectors**: Test against specific consumer versions
• **Tagging**: `prod`, `dev`, `feat/new-endpoint` tags in broker
• **Can-I-Deploy Gates**: Prevent deployment if contracts not verified

**Performance Optimization**:
• **Parallel Verification**: Run provider tests in parallel
• **Incremental Verification**: Only test changed contracts
• **Caching**: Cache provider states between tests
• **Selective Testing**: Test only relevant consumer versions

**Monitoring and Metrics**:
```prometheus
# Prometheus metrics for contract testing
pact_verification_total{provider, consumer, result="success"}
pact_verification_total{provider, consumer, result="failure"}
pact_verification_duration_seconds{provider, consumer}
pact_contracts_total{provider, consumer}
pact_broker_webhook_failures_total
```

content.caption: OpenAPI Contract Validation and Testing
content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
OpenAPI Contract Testing and Validation
Validates API implementation against OpenAPI specification
"""

import json
import yaml
import requests
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
import jsonschema
from jsonschema import validate
from deepdiff import DeepDiff
import re

class ValidationResult(Enum):
    PASS = "pass"
    FAIL = "fail"
    WARNING = "warning"

@dataclass
class ValidationIssue:
    endpoint: str
    method: str
    issue_type: str
    message: str
    severity: str  # error, warning, info
    details: Optional[Dict] = None

class OpenAPIValidator:
    """
    Validates API implementation against OpenAPI specification
    """
    
    def __init__(self, openapi_spec: Dict, base_url: str):
        self.spec = openapi_spec
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip('/')
        self.session = requests.Session()
        self.issues: List[ValidationIssue] = []
        
    def validate_all_endpoints(self) -> List[ValidationIssue]:
        """Validate all endpoints in the OpenAPI spec"""
        print(f"Validating API against OpenAPI specification")
        print(f"Base URL: {self.base_url}")
        print(f"Title: {self.spec.get('info', {}).get('title')}")
        print(f"Version: {self.spec.get('info', {}).get('version')}")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        # Validate specification structure first
        self._validate_spec_structure()
        
        # Validate each endpoint
        paths = self.spec.get('paths', {})
        
        for path, path_item in paths.items():
            for method, operation in path_item.items():
                if method in ['get', 'post', 'put', 'patch', 'delete', 'head', 'options']:
                    self._validate_endpoint(path, method.upper(), operation)
        
        return self.issues
    
    def _validate_endpoint(self, path: str, method: str, operation: Dict):
        """Validate a single endpoint"""
        operation_id = operation.get('operationId', f'{method} {path}')
        print(f"Validating: {method} {path} ({operation_id})")
        
        # 1. Test endpoint existence
        self._test_endpoint_exists(path, method, operation)
        
        # 2. Validate request parameters
        self._validate_parameters(path, method, operation)
        
        # 3. Validate request body schema if present
        self._validate_request_body(path, method, operation)
        
        # 4. Validate response schemas
        self._validate_responses(path, method, operation)
        
    def _test_endpoint_exists(self, path: str, method: str, operation: Dict):
        """Test if endpoint exists and returns expected status code"""
        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
        
        # Get expected successful response codes
        expected_codes = list(operation.get('responses', {}).keys())
        if not expected_codes:
            self._add_issue(path, method, "missing_responses", 
                          "No response codes defined in OpenAPI spec", "warning")
            return
        
        # Try to make request (without body for now)
        try:
            response = self.session.request(
                method, url, 
                timeout=10,
                allow_redirects=False
            )
            
            # Check if status code is documented
            status_str = str(response.status_code)
            if status_str not in expected_codes:
                self._add_issue(path, method, "unexpected_status",
                              f"Got status {response.status_code}, expected one of {expected_codes}",
                              "error",
                              {"actual": response.status_code, "expected": expected_codes})
            
        except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
            self._add_issue(path, method, "connection_error",
                          f"Could not connect to endpoint", "error")
        except Exception as e:
            self._add_issue(path, method, "request_error",
                          f"Request failed: {str(e)}", "error")
    
    def _validate_parameters(self, path: str, method: str, operation: Dict):
        """Validate that parameters match specification"""
        parameters = operation.get('parameters', [])
        
        for param in parameters:
            param_name = param.get('name')
            param_in = param.get('in')  # query, path, header, cookie
            required = param.get('required', False)
            
            if param_in == 'path':
                # Check path parameter exists in path template
                if param_name not in path:
                    self._add_issue(path, method, "missing_path_param",
                                  f"Path parameter '{param_name}' not found in path template",
                                  "error", {"parameter": param})
            
            # TODO: Test parameter validation
            # This would require making actual requests with different parameter values
    
    def _validate_request_body(self, path: str, method: str, operation: Dict):
        """Validate request body schema"""
        request_body = operation.get('requestBody')
        
        if not request_body:
            return
        
        content = request_body.get('content', {})
        
        # Check if any content type is specified
        if not content:
            self._add_issue(path, method, "empty_request_body",
                          "Request body defined but no content types specified",
                          "warning")
            return
        
        # For JSON content, validate schema
        if 'application/json' in content:
            json_schema = content['application/json'].get('schema')
            if json_schema:
                # Generate example from schema
                example = self._generate_example_from_schema(json_schema)
                
                # Try to make request with example
                self._test_request_with_body(path, method, json_schema, example)
    
    def _validate_responses(self, path: str, method: str, operation: Dict):
        """Validate response schemas"""
        responses = operation.get('responses', {})
        
        for status_code, response in responses.items():
            # Skip wildcard status codes for now
            if status_code == 'default':
                continue
                
            content = response.get('content', {})
            
            if 'application/json' in content:
                json_schema = content['application/json'].get('schema')
                if json_schema:
                    # Try to get actual response and validate against schema
                    self._test_response_schema(path, method, status_code, json_schema)
    
    def _test_response_schema(self, path: str, method: str, 
                            expected_status: str, schema: Dict):
        """Test actual response against JSON schema"""
        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
        
        # Replace path parameters with test values
        url = self._replace_path_parameters(url)
        
        try:
            response = self.session.request(method, url, timeout=10)
            
            # Check if we got the expected status
            if str(response.status_code) == expected_status:
                # Validate response body against schema
                if response.content:
                    try:
                        response_json = response.json()
                        self._validate_against_schema(response_json, schema, path, method)
                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
                        self._add_issue(path, method, "invalid_json_response",
                                      f"Response is not valid JSON for status {expected_status}",
                                      "error")
            
        except Exception as e:
            # Don't add issue for connection errors - already handled elsewhere
            pass
    
    def _validate_against_schema(self, data: Any, schema: Dict, 
                               path: str, method: str):
        """Validate data against JSON schema"""
        try:
            validate(instance=data, schema=schema)
        except jsonschema.ValidationError as e:
            self._add_issue(path, method, "schema_validation_error",
                          f"Response does not match schema: {e.message}",
                          "error",
                          {"validation_error": str(e), "path": e.json_path})
        except jsonschema.SchemaError as e:
            self._add_issue(path, method, "invalid_schema",
                          f"Invalid JSON schema: {e.message}",
                          "error")
    
    def _test_request_with_body(self, path: str, method: str, 
                              schema: Dict, example: Dict):
        """Test request with example body"""
        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
        url = self._replace_path_parameters(url)
        
        # Only test POST, PUT, PATCH methods with body
        if method not in ['POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH']:
            return
        
        try:
            response = self.session.request(
                method, url,
                json=example,
                timeout=10
            )
            
            # Check if request was accepted (2xx or 4xx for invalid data)
            if response.status_code >= 400:
                # Parse error response if possible
                try:
                    error_data = response.json()
                    # Could validate error response against schema if defined
                except:
                    pass
            
        except Exception as e:
            # Silently fail - this is just a test
            pass
    
    def _replace_path_parameters(self, path: str) -> str:
        """Replace path parameters with test values"""
        # Simple replacement - in real implementation, use parameter examples
        replacements = {
            '{productId}': '123',
            '{userId}': '456',
            '{orderId}': '789',
            '{id}': '1'
        }
        
        for param, value in replacements.items():
            path = path.replace(param, value)
        
        return path
    
    def _generate_example_from_schema(self, schema: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Generate example data from JSON schema"""
        # Simple example generator
        # In production, use a library like json-schema-faker
        
        example = {}
        properties = schema.get('properties', {})
        required = schema.get('required', [])
        
        for prop_name, prop_schema in properties.items():
            if prop_name in required or len(required) == 0:
                prop_type = prop_schema.get('type')
                
                if prop_type == 'string':
                    if 'format' in prop_schema:
                        if prop_schema['format'] == 'uuid':
                            example[prop_name] = '123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000'
                        elif prop_schema['format'] == 'email':
                            example[prop_name] = 'test@example.com'
                        elif prop_schema['format'] == 'date-time':
                            example[prop_name] = '2024-01-25T10:30:00Z'
                        else:
                            example[prop_name] = 'example-string'
                    elif 'enum' in prop_schema:
                        example[prop_name] = prop_schema['enum'][0]
                    else:
                        example[prop_name] = 'example-value'
                
                elif prop_type == 'number' or prop_type == 'integer':
                    example[prop_name] = 42
                
                elif prop_type == 'boolean':
                    example[prop_name] = True
                
                elif prop_type == 'array':
                    items_schema = prop_schema.get('items', {})
                    item_example = self._generate_example_from_schema(items_schema)
                    example[prop_name] = [item_example]
                
                elif prop_type == 'object':
                    example[prop_name] = self._generate_example_from_schema(prop_schema)
        
        return example
    
    def _validate_spec_structure(self):
        """Validate OpenAPI specification structure"""
        required_fields = ['openapi', 'info', 'paths']
        
        for field in required_fields:
            if field not in self.spec:
                self._add_issue('', '', 'invalid_spec',
                              f"Missing required field in OpenAPI spec: {field}",
                              "error")
        
        # Check info object
        info = self.spec.get('info', {})
        if 'title' not in info:
            self._add_issue('', '', 'invalid_spec_info',
                          "Missing 'title' in info object", "warning")
        if 'version' not in info:
            self._add_issue('', '', 'invalid_spec_info',
                          "Missing 'version' in info object", "warning")
    
    def _add_issue(self, endpoint: str, method: str, issue_type: str,
                  message: str, severity: str, details: Optional[Dict] = None):
        """Add a validation issue"""
        issue = ValidationIssue(
            endpoint=endpoint,
            method=method,
            issue_type=issue_type,
            message=message,
            severity=severity,
            details=details
        )
        self.issues.append(issue)
        
        # Print issue
        severity_icon = {"error": "❌", "warning": "⚠️", "info": "ℹ️"}.get(severity, "")
        print(f"  {severity_icon} [{severity.upper()}] {message}")
    
    def generate_report(self) -> Dict:
        """Generate validation report"""
        errors = [i for i in self.issues if i.severity == 'error']
        warnings = [i for i in self.issues if i.severity == 'warning']
        
        return {
            'summary': {
                'total_issues': len(self.issues),
                'errors': len(errors),
                'warnings': len(warnings),
                'endpoints_tested': len(set(f"{i.method} {i.endpoint}" for i in self.issues))
            },
            'issues': [
                {
                    'endpoint': i.endpoint,
                    'method': i.method,
                    'type': i.issue_type,
                    'message': i.message,
                    'severity': i.severity,
                    'details': i.details
                }
                for i in self.issues
            ],
            'recommendations': self._generate_recommendations()
        }
    
    def _generate_recommendations(self) -> List[str]:
        """Generate recommendations based on issues found"""
        recommendations = []
        
        error_types = set(i.issue_type for i in self.issues if i.severity == 'error')
        
        if 'missing_path_param' in error_types:
            recommendations.append("Ensure path parameters in OpenAPI spec match actual path templates")
        
        if 'schema_validation_error' in error_types:
            recommendations.append("Update API implementation to match response schemas in OpenAPI spec")
        
        if 'unexpected_status' in error_types:
            recommendations.append("Document all possible response status codes in OpenAPI spec")
        
        # General recommendations
        recommendations.extend([
            "Use OpenAPI linter (Spectral) to validate specification quality",
            "Generate API clients from OpenAPI spec to ensure consistency",
            "Implement automated contract testing in CI/CD pipeline",
            "Use semantic versioning for API changes"
        ])
        
        return list(set(recommendations))

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Load OpenAPI spec
    with open('openapi.yaml', 'r') as f:
        spec = yaml.safe_load(f)
    
    # Create validator
    validator = OpenAPIValidator(
        openapi_spec=spec,
        base_url='http://localhost:8080'
    )
    
    # Run validation
    issues = validator.validate_all_endpoints()
    report = validator.generate_report()
    
    # Print summary
    summary = report['summary']
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("VALIDATION SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Endpoints Tested: {summary['endpoints_tested']}")
    print(f"Total Issues: {summary['total_issues']}")
    print(f"Errors: {summary['errors']}")
    print(f"Warnings: {summary['warnings']}")
    
    # Print recommendations
    if report['recommendations']:
        print("\nRECOMMENDATIONS:")
        for i, rec in enumerate(report['recommendations'], 1):
            print(f"  {i}. {rec}")
    
    # Save report
    with open('openapi-validation-report.json', 'w') as f:
        json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
    
    print("\nDetailed report saved to: openapi-validation-report.json")

items.reality: Pact supports multiple languages. Teams can use different languages as long as they can publish/verify pacts

content.title: SOAP Protocol Architecture
content.explanation:
SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) is an XML-based protocol for exchanging structured information in web services. Unlike REST which uses standard HTTP methods, SOAP defines its own XML message format that can be transported via HTTP, SMTP, TCP, and other protocols.

**Key Components**:
• **Envelope**: Root element defining the XML document as a SOAP message
• **Header**: Optional element containing application-specific information like authentication, transaction management
• **Body**: Required element containing the actual message data
• **Fault**: Optional element for error messages when something goes wrong

**SOAP Message Example**:
```xml
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope">
  <soap:Header>
    <!-- Security, transaction info -->
  </soap:Header>
  <soap:Body>
    <!-- Actual request/response data -->
    <m:GetProduct xmlns:m="http://example.com/products">
      <m:productId>12345</m:productId>
    </m:GetProduct>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

**Why SOAP Still Matters**:
While REST APIs dominate modern web services, SOAP remains critical in:
• **Enterprise systems**: Banking, healthcare, government
• **Legacy integrations**: Systems built before REST became popular
• **WS-* standards**: Advanced features like WS-Security, WS-Transactions
• **Contract-first development**: Strict WSDL contracts ensure compatibility

content.title: WSDL: The SOAP Service Contract
content.explanation:
WSDL (Web Services Description Language) is an XML document that describes a web service. It acts as a contract between service provider and consumer.

**WSDL Structure**:
1. **Types**: XML Schema definitions for data types
2. **Messages**: Definitions of the data being communicated
3. **Port Types**: Abstract operations (similar to interfaces)
4. **Bindings**: Protocol-specific details for each port type
5. **Services**: Collection of related endpoints

**Why WSDL Matters for Testing**:
• **Automatic Test Generation**: Tools can generate tests from WSDL
• **Contract Validation**: Ensure implementation matches specification
• **Client Generation**: Generate client code in multiple languages
• **Change Detection**: Identify breaking changes in service updates

**Common WSDL Patterns**:
• **Document/Literal Wrapped**: Most common, uses XML schema types
• **RPC/Literal**: Remote procedure call style
• **Document/Literal**: Straight document style without wrapping

content.title: SOAP UI: The Complete Testing Solution
content.explanation:
SOAP UI is the industry-standard tool for SOAP API testing. It provides a comprehensive environment for functional, security, and performance testing.

**Key Features**:
• **WSDL Import**: Automatically generate tests from WSDL
• **Test Suites**: Organize tests hierarchically
• **Data-Driven Testing**: Use Excel, XML, JSON, databases as data sources
• **Assertions**: Validate responses with XPath, XQuery, script assertions
• **Mock Services**: Create mock SOAP services for testing clients
• **Security Testing**: Test WS-Security, SQL injection, XSS vulnerabilities

**Typical SOAP UI Workflow**:
1. Import WSDL to create project
2. Generate test suites from operations
3. Parameterize requests with test data
4. Add assertions to validate responses
5. Run tests and analyze results
6. Generate reports

**Advanced Features in ReadyAPI (SOAP UI Pro)**:
• **Load Testing**: Distributed performance testing
• **VirtServer**: Advanced service virtualization
• **Database Toolkit**: SQL query builder and validation
• **CI/CD Integration**: Jenkins, TeamCity plugins

content.title: Performance Testing SOAP Services
content.explanation:
SOAP performance testing is crucial because:
• **XML Processing Overhead**: XML parsing/generation is CPU-intensive
• **Message Size**: SOAP messages are larger than equivalent JSON
• **WS-Security**: Encryption/decryption adds significant overhead
• **Enterprise Scale**: SOAP services often handle critical business transactions

**Key Performance Metrics**:
• **Response Time**: P50, P90, P95, P99 percentiles
• **Throughput**: Requests per second/minute
• **Error Rate**: Percentage of failed requests
• **Concurrent Users**: Maximum users without degradation
• **Resource Usage**: CPU, memory, network consumption

**Performance Testing Tools**:
• **ReadyAPI Load Testing**: Integrated with SOAP UI
• **JMeter SOAP Sampler**: Open-source option
• **Gatling**: High-performance load testing
• **Custom Scripts**: Python/Java with concurrency

**Common Performance Issues**:
• **XML Parsing Bottlenecks**: Slow XML processors
• **Memory Leaks**: XML DOM not properly released
• **Connection Pool Exhaustion**: Database/connection limits
• **WS-Security Overhead**: Cryptographic operations slowing responses

      <minTPS>10</minTPS> <!-- At least 10 TPS -->

content.title: The Evolution of API Test Architecture
content.explanation:
API test architecture has evolved from simple script-based approaches to sophisticated, scalable frameworks. Understanding this evolution helps design better architectures:

**Generation 1: Script-Based Testing**
• **Characteristics**: Hardcoded values, no abstraction, duplicate code
• **Problems**: Brittle tests, high maintenance, difficult to scale

**Generation 2: Modular Testing**
• **Characteristics**: Basic functions, some reuse, simple assertions
• **Improvements**: Reduced duplication, easier maintenance

**Generation 3: Framework-Based Testing**
• **Characteristics**: Design patterns, configuration files, reporting
• **Improvements**: Scalability, maintainability, reusability

**Generation 4: Platform-Based Testing**
• **Characteristics**: Self-service platforms, AI-assisted, cloud-native
• **Improvements**: Democratization, intelligent testing, global scale

**Modern API Test Architecture Goals**:
1. **Scalability**: Handle thousands of tests across teams
2. **Maintainability**: Easy updates when APIs change
3. **Reusability**: Share components across test suites
4. **Reliability**: Consistent, flake-free test execution
5. **Observability**: Comprehensive logging and reporting
6. **Integration**: Seamless CI/CD pipeline integration

content.title: Layered Test Architecture (Onion Architecture)
content.explanation:
The layered architecture separates concerns into distinct layers, each with specific responsibilities:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Test Layers"
        L1[Test Execution Layer] --> L2[Test Business Layer]
        L2 --> L3[API Service Layer]
        L3 --> L4[Client Layer]
        L4 --> L5[Infrastructure Layer]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cross-Cutting Concerns"
        CC1[Configuration]
        CC2[Logging]
        CC3[Reporting]
        CC4[Test Data]
    end
    
    L1 --> CC1
    L2 --> CC2
    L3 --> CC3
    L4 --> CC4
```

**Layer 1: Infrastructure Layer**
• **Purpose**: Lowest-level communication (HTTP client, database connections)
• **Responsibilities**: Raw HTTP requests, connection management, retry logic
• **Example**: `HttpClient`, `DatabaseConnection`, `MessageQueueClient`

**Layer 2: Client Layer**
• **Purpose**: API-specific clients with business logic
• **Responsibilities**: Endpoint mapping, request/response models, basic validation
• **Example**: `UserServiceClient`, `OrderServiceClient`, `ProductServiceClient`

**Layer 3: API Service Layer**
• **Purpose**: Business operations and workflows
• **Responsibilities**: Complex API interactions, multi-step operations
• **Example**: `UserRegistrationService`, `OrderProcessingService`, `PaymentService`

**Layer 4: Test Business Layer**
• **Purpose**: Test-specific business logic and assertions
• **Responsibilities**: Test data preparation, complex assertions, test scenarios
• **Example**: `UserTestValidator`, `OrderTestVerifier`, `PerformanceTestRunner`

**Layer 5: Test Execution Layer**
• **Purpose**: Test cases and test suites
• **Responsibilities**: Test methods, test lifecycle management, reporting hooks
• **Example**: `UserRegistrationTests`, `OrderProcessingTests`, `SecurityTests`

**Cross-Cutting Concerns**:
• **Configuration**: Environment-specific settings
• **Logging**: Structured logging across all layers
• **Reporting**: Test execution reports
• **Test Data**: Test data management and generation

content.title: Page Object Model for APIs (Service Object Pattern)
content.explanation:
Adapting the Page Object Model (POM) for APIs creates the Service Object Pattern, which provides:

**Core Principles**:
1. **Encapsulation**: Hide API implementation details from tests
2. **Reusability**: Service objects can be reused across multiple tests
3. **Maintainability**: Changes to API affect only service objects, not tests
4. **Readability**: Tests read like business requirements, not technical implementations

**Service Object Components**:
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Service Object Structure"
        A[Service Interface] --> B[Service Implementation]
        B --> C[Request Builder]
        B --> D[Response Validator]
        B --> E[DTO Models]
    end
    
    F[Test Class] --> A
```

**Benefits over Traditional API Testing**:
• **Test Stability**: Isolate tests from API changes
• **Team Collaboration**: Business analysts can understand test scenarios
• **Code Organization**: Logical grouping of related API operations
• **Parallel Development**: Teams can work on services and tests independently

**Implementation Guidelines**:
1. **One Service Object per API Resource**: `UserService`, `OrderService`, `ProductService`
2. **Business-Focused Methods**: `createUser()`, `placeOrder()`, `updateProductInventory()`
3. **Built-in Validation**: Service objects should validate responses
4. **Error Handling**: Consistent error handling across all service objects
5. **Configuration Integration**: Environment-aware service objects

content.title: Factory and Builder Patterns in Test Automation
content.explanation:
Design patterns like Factory and Builder are essential for creating flexible, maintainable test frameworks.

**Factory Pattern for Test Objects**:
• **Purpose**: Create objects without specifying exact class
• **Use Cases**: Creating different types of users, orders, products
• **Benefits**: Decouples object creation from usage, simplifies test setup

**Builder Pattern for Complex Objects**:
• **Purpose**: Construct complex objects step by step
• **Use Cases**: Building complex API requests, test data entities
• **Benefits**: Improves readability, handles optional parameters gracefully

**Strategy Pattern for Test Execution**:
• **Purpose**: Define family of algorithms, make them interchangeable
• **Use Cases**: Different validation strategies, multiple assertion approaches
• **Benefits**: Flexible test execution, easy to add new strategies

**Template Method Pattern for Test Flows**:
• **Purpose**: Define skeleton of algorithm, let subclasses override steps
• **Use Cases**: Standard test workflows with variations
• **Benefits**: Code reuse, consistent test structure

**Practical Application**:
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Patterns in Test Framework"
        A[Test Data Factory] --> B[Creates]
        B --> C[User Objects]
        B --> D[Order Objects]
        B --> E[Product Objects]
        
        F[Request Builder] --> G[Builds]
        G --> H[Simple Requests]
        G --> I[Complex Requests]
        
        J[Validation Strategy] --> K[Selects]
        K --> L[Schema Validation]
        K --> M[Business Rule Validation]
        K --> N[Performance Validation]
    end

content.title: Comprehensive Test Data Management
content.explanation:
Effective test data management is critical for reliable API testing. A robust strategy includes:

**Test Data Lifecycle**:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Data Generation] --> B[Data Storage]
    B --> C[Data Retrieval]
    C --> D[Data Usage]
    D --> E[Data Cleanup]
    E --> A
```

**Data Generation Strategies**:
1. **Static Test Data**: Pre-defined data in files (JSON, CSV, SQL)
2. **Dynamic Test Data**: Generated at runtime using libraries (Faker, Bogus)
3. **Synthetic Test Data**: Realistic but fake data for testing
4. **Production-like Data**: Anonymized production data

**Data Management Patterns**:
• **Test Data Factory**: Centralized data creation
• **Builder Pattern**: Complex object construction
• **Object Mother**: Pre-configured valid/invalid objects
• **Test Data Repository**: Storage and retrieval abstraction

**Data Isolation Strategies**:
• **Database Per Test**: Clean isolation but resource-intensive
• **Transaction Rollback**: Fast but database-specific
• **Data Cleanup Hooks**: Custom cleanup after tests
• **Parallel Data Sets**: Unique data for parallel execution

**Challenges and Solutions**:
• **Data Dependency**: Use data setup/teardown hooks
• **Data Consistency**: Implement data validation rules
• **Performance**: Cache frequently used data
• **Maintenance**: Version control test data

content.title: Environment Configuration Strategy
content.explanation:
A robust environment configuration strategy ensures tests run consistently across different environments while maintaining security and flexibility.

**Configuration Hierarchy**:
```mermaid
graph TB
    A[Default Config] --> B[Environment Config]
    B --> C[User Config]
    C --> D[Runtime Overrides]
    D --> E[Final Configuration]
```

**Configuration Sources (in order of precedence)**:
1. **Command Line Arguments**: Highest priority, runtime overrides
2. **Environment Variables**: System-level configuration
3. **Configuration Files**: Environment-specific files
4. **Default Properties**: Framework defaults

**Environment Types**:
• **Local/Dev**: For developer machines, may have mock services
• **CI/CD**: Automated testing environments
• **Staging/UAT**: Pre-production, mirrors production
• **Production**: Real environment, read-only or limited testing

**Security Considerations**:
• **Secrets Management**: Never commit secrets to source control
• **Encryption**: Encrypt sensitive configuration
• **Access Control**: Restrict configuration access based on role
• **Audit Logging**: Track configuration changes

**Best Practices**:
1. **Externalize Configuration**: Keep config outside code
2. **Environment-Specific Files**: Separate config per environment
3. **Validation**: Validate configuration at startup
4. **Documentation**: Document all configuration options
5. **Version Control**: Version control non-sensitive config

content.title: Advanced Reporting and Logging Implementation
content.explanation:
Comprehensive reporting and logging are essential for debugging, monitoring, and communicating test results.

**Logging Strategy**:
• **Structured Logging**: JSON format for easy parsing and analysis
• **Log Levels**: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR with appropriate usage
• **Contextual Information**: Include test name, execution ID, timestamps
• **Performance Logging**: Track execution times, memory usage
• **Distributed Tracing**: Trace requests across multiple services

**Reporting Components**:
1. **Execution Reports**: Test pass/fail status, duration
2. **Performance Reports**: Response times, throughput, resource usage
3. **Coverage Reports**: API endpoint coverage, scenario coverage
4. **Trend Reports**: Historical performance and stability trends
5. **Compliance Reports**: Security, accessibility, compliance checks

**Report Formats**:
• **HTML**: Human-readable, interactive reports
• **JSON**: Machine-readable for further processing
• **JUnit XML**: Standard format for CI/CD integration
• **PDF**: Printable, formal reports
• **Custom Formats**: Integration with custom dashboards

**Notification Strategies**:
• **Email Notifications**: Test execution summaries
• **Slack/Teams Integration**: Real-time notifications
• **Webhook Callbacks**: Integration with monitoring systems
• **Dashboard Updates**: Real-time dashboards

content.title: CI/CD Pipeline Integration
content.explanation:
Integrating API tests into CI/CD pipelines ensures continuous validation and provides fast feedback to developers.

**Pipeline Stages for API Testing**:
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "CI/CD Pipeline"
        A[Code Commit] --> B[Build & Package]
        B --> C[Unit Tests]
        C --> D[API Contract Tests]
        D --> E[API Functional Tests]
        E --> F[API Integration Tests]
        F --> G[API Performance Tests]
        G --> H[Security Tests]
        H --> I[Deploy to Staging]
        I --> J[API Regression Tests]
        J --> K[Deploy to Production]

```

**Key Integration Points**:
1. **Trigger Tests Automatically**: On pull requests, merges, schedules
2. **Parallel Test Execution**: Reduce feedback time
3. **Test Result Analysis**: Automated analysis and reporting
4. **Quality Gates**: Block deployments on test failures
5. **Artifact Management**: Store test reports and artifacts

**Infrastructure Considerations**:
• **Test Environment Management**: Automated environment provisioning
• **Test Data Management**: Isolated, reproducible test data
• **Service Virtualization**: Mock dependencies for isolated testing
• **Load Testing Infrastructure**: Scalable load testing resources

**Best Practices**:
• **Fast Feedback**: Keep test execution under 10 minutes
• **Reliable Tests**: Minimize flaky tests
• **Resource Efficiency**: Clean up resources after tests
• **Security**: Secure credentials and sensitive data
• **Monitoring**: Monitor test execution and resource usage

GitHub Actions Workflow for API Testing
content.code:
# .github/workflows/api-tests.yml
name: API Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'  # Daily at 2 AM

env:
  JAVA_VERSION: '11'
  MAVEN_VERSION: '3.8.4'
  TEST_ENVIRONMENT: 'ci'
  
jobs:
  unit-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Set up Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        distribution: 'temurin'
    
    - name: Cache Maven dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: ~/.m2
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-m2-${{ hashFiles('**/pom.xml') }}
        restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-m2-
    
    - name: Run unit tests
      run: |
        mvn test \
          -Dtest=*UnitTest \
          -Denvironment=${{ env.TEST_ENVIRONMENT }} \
          -Dparallel.threads=4
      env:
        API_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.API_BASE_URL }}
    
    - name: Upload unit test results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      if: always()
      with:
        name: unit-test-results
        path: target/surefire-reports/
    
  functional-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: unit-tests
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        test-suite: [users, orders, products, payments]
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Set up Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        distribution: 'temurin'
    
    - name: Cache Maven dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: ~/.m2
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-m2-${{ hashFiles('**/pom.xml') }}
        restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-m2-
    
    - name: Run functional tests
      run: |
        mvn test \
          -Dtest=*${{ matrix.test-suite }}*FunctionalTest \
          -Denvironment=${{ env.TEST_ENVIRONMENT }} \
          -Dparallel.threads=2
      env:
        API_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.API_BASE_URL }}
        API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.API_CLIENT_ID }}
        API_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.API_CLIENT_SECRET }}
    
    - name: Upload test results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      if: always()
      with:
        name: functional-test-results-${{ matrix.test-suite }}
        path: target/failsafe-reports/
    
  integration-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: functional-tests
    
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:14
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: testdb
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
      
      redis:
        image: redis:7
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Set up Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        distribution: 'temurin'
    
    - name: Start application
      run: |
        docker-compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d
        sleep 30
        curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1
    
    - name: Run integration tests
      run: |
        mvn test \
          -Dtest=*IntegrationTest \
          -Denvironment=${{ env.TEST_ENVIRONMENT }} \
          -Dapi.baseUrl=http://localhost:8080
      env:
        DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/testdb
        DB_USERNAME: postgres
        DB_PASSWORD: postgres
        REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379
    
    - name: Stop application
      if: always()
      run: docker-compose -f docker-compose.test.yml down
    
    - name: Upload integration test results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      if: always()
      with:
        name: integration-test-results
        path: target/failsafe-reports/
    
  performance-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: integration-tests
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Set up Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        distribution: 'temurin'
    
    - name: Run performance tests
      run: |
        mvn gatling:test \
          -Dgatling.simulationClass=com.company.api.performance.LoadTest \
          -Denvironment=perf \
          -Dusers=50 \
          -Dduration=60
      env:
        API_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.PERF_API_BASE_URL }}
    
    - name: Upload performance report
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      if: always()
      with:
        name: performance-report
        path: target/gatling/
    
    - name: Upload performance results to dashboard
      run: |
        curl -X POST https://dashboard.company.com/api/performance \
          -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
          -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.DASHBOARD_TOKEN }}" \
          -d @target/gatling/latest/simulation.log
    
  quality-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [unit-tests, functional-tests, integration-tests]
    if: always()
    
    steps:
    - name: Download all test results
      uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
      with:
        path: test-results
    
    - name: Analyze test results
      run: |
        # Aggregate test results
        python scripts/analyze_test_results.py \
          --input-dir test-results \
          --output-file quality-report.json
        
        # Check quality metrics
        python scripts/check_quality_gate.py \
          --report quality-report.json \
          --min-pass-rate 95 \
          --max-failures 5
      
    - name: Generate test report
      if: always()
      uses: dorny/test-reporter@v1
      with:
        name: Test Results
        path: test-results/**/*.xml
        reporter: java-junit
    
    - name: Send Slack notification
      if: failure()
      uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
      with:
        status: failure
        fields: repo,message,commit,author,action,eventName,ref,workflow,job,took
      env:
        SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
    
  deploy-staging:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    if: success() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Deploy to staging
      run: |
        # Deploy application
        ./scripts/deploy.sh staging
        
        # Run smoke tests
        ./scripts/run_smoke_tests.sh staging
      env:
        DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.STAGING_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
        
    - name: Run regression tests
      run: |
        mvn test \
          -Dtest=*RegressionTest \
          -Denvironment=staging \
          -Dapi.baseUrl=${{ secrets.STAGING_API_URL }}
      env:
        API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.STAGING_API_CLIENT_ID }}
        API_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.STAGING_API_CLIENT_SECRET }}

  deploy-production:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: deploy-staging
    if: success() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://api.company.com
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Deploy to production
      run: |
        # Deploy with canary strategy
        ./scripts/deploy_production.sh \
          --canary \
          --percentage 10
      env:
        DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
        
    - name: Run production smoke tests
      run: |
        ./scripts/run_smoke_tests.sh production
      env:
        API_BASE_URL: https://api.company.com
        API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_API_CLIENT_ID }}
        API_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_API_CLIENT_SECRET }}
        
    - name: Monitor canary deployment
      run: |
        # Monitor metrics for canary deployment
        ./scripts/monitor_canary.sh \
          --duration 300 \
          --error-threshold 1
      
    - name: Complete deployment
      if: success()
      run: |
        # Complete canary deployment
        ./scripts/complete_deployment.sh

content.title: Performance Testing Spectrum
content.explanation:
Performance testing is not a single activity but a spectrum of tests that validate different aspects of system behavior under various conditions. Understanding when to use each type is crucial for comprehensive performance validation.

**The Performance Testing Pyramid**:
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Performance Test Types"
        A[Load Testing] --> B[Stress Testing]
        B --> C[Spike Testing]
        C --> D[Endurance Testing]
        D --> E[Volume Testing]
        E --> F[Scalability Testing]
    end
    
    subgraph "Frequency"
        G[Daily/Continuous] --> A
        H[Weekly/Sprint] --> B
        I[Release Cycle] --> C
        J[Quarterly] --> D
        K[Major Releases] --> E
        L[Architecture Changes] --> F
    end
```

**Load Testing Deep Dive**:
Load testing answers the question: "Can the system handle the expected number of users?"
• **Key Characteristics**: Simulates normal/peak expected load
• **When to Use**: Before major releases, capacity planning
• **Common Patterns**: Ramp-up, steady-state, ramp-down
• **Success Criteria**: Meet response time SLAs, maintain throughput

**Stress Testing Deep Dive**:
Stress testing pushes the system beyond its limits to understand failure modes.
• **Key Characteristics**: Incremental load increase beyond capacity
• **When to Use**: Disaster recovery planning, understanding limits
• **Critical Findings**: Breaking points, error handling, recovery
• **Warning Signs**: Memory leaks, thread deadlocks, resource exhaustion

**Spike Testing Importance**:
Spike testing validates the system's ability to handle sudden, unexpected load increases.
• **Real-World Examples**: Social media mentions, breaking news, flash sales
• **Key Metrics**: Response time degradation, error rate spikes
• **Mitigation Strategies**: Auto-scaling, rate limiting, caching
• **Recovery Testing**: How quickly does the system recover after a spike?

**Endurance Testing for Stability**:
Also known as soak testing, endurance testing uncovers issues that only appear over time.
• **Common Issues Found**: Memory leaks, database connection leaks, log file growth
• **Duration Considerations**: Typically 8-72 hours, depending on business needs
• **Monitoring Focus**: Memory growth trends, throughput degradation
• **Cleanup Validation**: Verify resource cleanup after sustained load

**Volume Testing Strategy**:
Volume testing focuses on data-related performance rather than user load.
• **Data Growth Testing**: How does performance degrade as data grows?
• **Batch Processing**: Testing large data import/export operations
• **Database Performance**: Query optimization, indexing strategies
• **Storage Considerations**: Disk I/O, file system performance

**Scalability Testing Approaches**:
Scalability testing validates both horizontal and vertical scaling capabilities.
• **Horizontal Scaling**: Adding more instances/nodes
• **Vertical Scaling**: Increasing resources (CPU, memory) per instance
• **Scaling Efficiency**: Linear vs. sublinear scaling
• **Cost-Benefit Analysis**: Performance gains vs. infrastructure costs

content.title: Understanding Percentiles in Performance Testing
content.explanation:
Percentiles are arguably the most important metrics in performance testing because they tell you about real user experience, not just averages.

**Why Averages Lie**:
```
Example Response Times (ms): [100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100, 1000]
Average: 190ms
p95: 1000ms
```
The average suggests good performance, but 10% of users experience 10x slower response times!

**Common Percentile Thresholds**:
```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Response Times] --> B[Sort Ascending]
    B --> C[Calculate Positions]
    C --> D[Percentile Values]
    
    D --> E[p50: Median]
    D --> F[p90: Good]
    D --> G[p95: Acceptable]
    D --> H[p99: Worst-case]
```

**Industry Standard Percentiles**:
• **p50 (Median)**: The middle value - half faster, half slower
• **p90**: 90% of requests are faster than this - good user experience
• **p95**: 95% of requests are faster - acceptable for most applications
• **p99**: 99% of requests are faster - worst-case scenario
• **p99.9**: 99.9% of requests are faster - critical systems requirement

**Real-World Example**:
For an e-commerce checkout:
- **Target**: p95 response time < 2 seconds
- **Acceptable**: p95 < 3 seconds
- **Unacceptable**: p95 > 3 seconds

**Percentile Calculation Example**:
Given 1000 sorted response times:
- p95 position = 0.95 × 1000 = 950th value
- If the 950th value is 1800ms, then p95 = 1800ms

**Monitoring Percentiles in Production**:
• Use monitoring tools that support percentile calculations (Prometheus, Datadog)
• Track percentile trends over time
• Set alerts for percentile breaches
• Compare percentiles across different user segments

content.title: Performance Calculation Examples and Formulas
content.content:
**Throughput**:
Throughput = Total Successful Requests / Test Duration (seconds)
Example: 10,000 requests in 100 seconds = 100 requests/second

**Error Rate**:
Error Rate = (Failed Requests / Total Requests) × 100
Example: 50 failed out of 10,000 requests = 0.5% error rate

**Response Time Percentile**:
pX = Value at position (X/100 × N) in sorted response times
Where N = total number of requests

**Concurrency Calculation**:
Concurrent Users = (Total Users × Session Duration) / Think Time
Where:
- Total Users = Number of unique users
- Session Duration = Average session length in seconds
- Think Time = Time between requests in seconds

**Capacity Planning Formula**:
Required Instances = (Peak Requests/Second × p95 Response Time) / (Instance Capacity × Target Utilization)

**Apdex Score Calculation**:
Apdex = (Satisfied Count + Tolerating Count/2) / Total Samples
Where:
- Satisfied: Response time ≤ T (target threshold)
- Tolerating: T < Response time ≤ 4T
- Frustrated: Response time > 4T

**Resource Utilization Efficiency**:
Efficiency = Throughput / (CPU Utilization × Memory Utilization)
Higher efficiency = better resource utilization

**Cost-Per-Transaction**:
Cost/Transaction = (Infrastructure Cost) / (Monthly Transactions)
Useful for cloud cost optimization

content.caption: Performance Metrics Analysis Script
content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Performance Metrics Analysis Tool
Calculates key performance metrics from test results
"""

import json
import statistics
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Tuple
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

@dataclass
class PerformanceMetrics:
    """Container for performance metrics"""
    test_name: str
    timestamp: str
    total_requests: int
    successful_requests: int
    failed_requests: int
    total_duration_seconds: float
    response_times_ms: List[float]
    throughput_rps: float = 0.0
    error_rate_percent: float = 0.0
    avg_response_time_ms: float = 0.0
    min_response_time_ms: float = 0.0
    max_response_time_ms: float = 0.0
    p50_response_time_ms: float = 0.0
    p90_response_time_ms: float = 0.0
    p95_response_time_ms: float = 0.0
    p99_response_time_ms: float = 0.0
    apdex_score: float = 0.0
    
class PerformanceAnalyzer:
    """Analyzes performance test results"""
    
    def __init__(self, apdex_threshold_ms: float = 500):
        self.apdex_threshold = apdex_threshold_ms
    
    def calculate_metrics(self, test_results: Dict) -> PerformanceMetrics:
        """Calculate all performance metrics from test results"""
        metrics = PerformanceMetrics(
            test_name=test_results.get('test_name', 'Unknown'),
            timestamp=test_results.get('timestamp', datetime.now().isoformat()),
            total_requests=len(test_results.get('requests', [])),
            successful_requests=0,
            failed_requests=0,
            total_duration_seconds=test_results.get('duration_seconds', 0),
            response_times_ms=[]
        )
        
        # Extract response times and count successes/failures
        for request in test_results.get('requests', []):
            response_time = request.get('response_time_ms', 0)
            status = request.get('status', 'unknown')
            
            metrics.response_times_ms.append(response_time)
            
            if 200 <= status < 400:
                metrics.successful_requests += 1
            else:
                metrics.failed_requests += 1
        
        # Sort response times for percentile calculations
        sorted_times = sorted(metrics.response_times_ms)
        
        # Calculate basic metrics
        if metrics.total_duration_seconds > 0:
            metrics.throughput_rps = metrics.total_requests / metrics.total_duration_seconds
        
        if metrics.total_requests > 0:
            metrics.error_rate_percent = (metrics.failed_requests / metrics.total_requests) * 100
            
            if sorted_times:
                metrics.avg_response_time_ms = statistics.mean(sorted_times)
                metrics.min_response_time_ms = min(sorted_times)
                metrics.max_response_time_ms = max(sorted_times)
                
                # Calculate percentiles
                metrics.p50_response_time_ms = self._calculate_percentile(sorted_times, 50)
                metrics.p90_response_time_ms = self._calculate_percentile(sorted_times, 90)
                metrics.p95_response_time_ms = self._calculate_percentile(sorted_times, 95)
                metrics.p99_response_time_ms = self._calculate_percentile(sorted_times, 99)
                
                # Calculate Apdex score
                metrics.apdex_score = self._calculate_apdex(sorted_times)
        
        return metrics
    
    def _calculate_percentile(self, values: List[float], percentile: float) -> float:
        """Calculate percentile value from sorted list"""
        if not values:
            return 0.0
        
        k = (len(values) - 1) * (percentile / 100)
        f = int(k)
        c = int(k) + 1 if f < k else f
        
        if f >= len(values):
            return values[-1]
        if c >= len(values):
            return values[f]
        
        # Linear interpolation
        d0 = values[f] * (c - k)
        d1 = values[c] * (k - f)
        return d0 + d1
    
    def _calculate_apdex(self, response_times: List[float]) -> float:
        """Calculate Apdex score"""
        if not response_times:
            return 0.0
        
        satisfied = 0
        tolerating = 0
        frustrated = 0
        
        t = self.apdex_threshold  # Target threshold
        
        for rt in response_times:
            if rt <= t:
                satisfied += 1
            elif rt <= 4 * t:
                tolerating += 1
            else:
                frustrated += 1
        
        total = satisfied + tolerating + frustrated
        if total == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        return (satisfied + (tolerating / 2)) / total
    
    def analyze_performance_trend(self, metrics_list: List[PerformanceMetrics]) -> Dict:
        """Analyze performance trends across multiple test runs"""
        if not metrics_list:
            return {}
        
        trend_analysis = {
            'total_runs': len(metrics_list),
            'throughput_trend': [],
            'response_time_trend': [],
            'error_rate_trend': [],
            'apdex_trend': [],
            'summary': {}
        }
        
        # Extract trends
        for metrics in metrics_list:
            trend_analysis['throughput_trend'].append({
                'timestamp': metrics.timestamp,
                'value': metrics.throughput_rps
            })
            trend_analysis['response_time_trend'].append({
                'timestamp': metrics.timestamp,
                'p95': metrics.p95_response_time_ms,
                'avg': metrics.avg_response_time_ms
            })
            trend_analysis['error_rate_trend'].append({
                'timestamp': metrics.timestamp,
                'value': metrics.error_rate_percent
            })
            trend_analysis['apdex_trend'].append({
                'timestamp': metrics.timestamp,
                'value': metrics.apdex_score
            })
        
        # Calculate summary statistics
        throughput_values = [m.throughput_rps for m in metrics_list]
        p95_values = [m.p95_response_time_ms for m in metrics_list]
        error_values = [m.error_rate_percent for m in metrics_list]
        apdex_values = [m.apdex_score for m in metrics_list]
        
        trend_analysis['summary'] = {
            'avg_throughput': statistics.mean(throughput_values) if throughput_values else 0,
            'avg_p95_response_time': statistics.mean(p95_values) if p95_values else 0,
            'avg_error_rate': statistics.mean(error_values) if error_values else 0,
            'avg_apdex': statistics.mean(apdex_values) if apdex_values else 0,
            'throughput_variance': statistics.variance(throughput_values) if len(throughput_values) > 1 else 0,
            'response_time_variance': statistics.variance(p95_values) if len(p95_values) > 1 else 0,
        }
        
        return trend_analysis
    
    def generate_report(self, metrics: PerformanceMetrics, output_format: str = 'text') -> str:
        """Generate performance report"""
        if output_format == 'json':
            return json.dumps(self._metrics_to_dict(metrics), indent=2)
        else:
            return self._generate_text_report(metrics)
    
    def _metrics_to_dict(self, metrics: PerformanceMetrics) -> Dict:
        """Convert metrics to dictionary"""
        return {
            'test_name': metrics.test_name,
            'timestamp': metrics.timestamp,
            'requests': {
                'total': metrics.total_requests,
                'successful': metrics.successful_requests,
                'failed': metrics.failed_requests,
                'error_rate_percent': round(metrics.error_rate_percent, 2)
            },
            'throughput': {
                'requests_per_second': round(metrics.throughput_rps, 2),
                'test_duration_seconds': round(metrics.total_duration_seconds, 2)
            },
            'response_times_ms': {
                'average': round(metrics.avg_response_time_ms, 2),
                'minimum': round(metrics.min_response_time_ms, 2),
                'maximum': round(metrics.max_response_time_ms, 2),
                'p50': round(metrics.p50_response_time_ms, 2),
                'p90': round(metrics.p90_response_time_ms, 2),
                'p95': round(metrics.p95_response_time_ms, 2),
                'p99': round(metrics.p99_response_time_ms, 2)
            },
            'user_experience': {
                'apdex_score': round(metrics.apdex_score, 3),
                'apdex_threshold_ms': self.apdex_threshold,
                'apdex_interpretation': self._interpret_apdex(metrics.apdex_score)
            }
        }
    
    def _generate_text_report(self, metrics: PerformanceMetrics) -> str:
        """Generate human-readable text report"""
        report = []
        report.append("=" * 60)
        report.append(f"PERFORMANCE TEST REPORT: {metrics.test_name}")
        report.append(f"Timestamp: {metrics.timestamp}")
        report.append("=" * 60)
        report.append("")
        
        # Requests Summary
        report.append("REQUESTS SUMMARY:")
        report.append("-" * 40)
        report.append(f"Total Requests: {metrics.total_requests:,}")
        report.append(f"Successful: {metrics.successful_requests:,} ({metrics.successful_requests/metrics.total_requests*100:.1f}%)")
        report.append(f"Failed: {metrics.failed_requests:,} ({metrics.error_rate_percent:.2f}%)")
        report.append(f"Test Duration: {metrics.total_duration_seconds:.2f} seconds")
        report.append("")
        
        # Throughput
        report.append("THROUGHPUT:")
        report.append("-" * 40)
        report.append(f"Requests per second: {metrics.throughput_rps:.2f}")
        report.append(f"Requests per minute: {metrics.throughput_rps * 60:.2f}")
        report.append(f"Requests per hour: {metrics.throughput_rps * 3600:,.0f}")
        report.append("")
        
        # Response Times
        report.append("RESPONSE TIMES (ms):")
        report.append("-" * 40)
        report.append(f"Average: {metrics.avg_response_time_ms:.2f}")
        report.append(f"Minimum: {metrics.min_response_time_ms:.2f}")
        report.append(f"Maximum: {metrics.max_response_time_ms:.2f}")
        report.append(f"p50 (Median): {metrics.p50_response_time_ms:.2f}")
        report.append(f"p90: {metrics.p90_response_time_ms:.2f}")
        report.append(f"p95: {metrics.p95_response_time_ms:.2f}")
        report.append(f"p99: {metrics.p99_response_time_ms:.2f}")
        report.append("")
        
        # User Experience
        report.append("USER EXPERIENCE:")
        report.append("-" * 40)
        report.append(f"Apdex Score: {metrics.apdex_score:.3f}")
        report.append(f"Apdex Interpretation: {self._interpret_apdex(metrics.apdex_score)}")
        report.append(f"Threshold: {self.apdex_threshold} ms (satisfied)")
        report.append(f"Tolerating threshold: {self.apdex_threshold * 4} ms")
        report.append("")
        
        # Performance Evaluation
        report.append("PERFORMANCE EVALUATION:")
        report.append("-" * 40)
        report.append(self._evaluate_performance(metrics))
        report.append("=" * 60)
        
        return '\n'.join(report)
    
    def _interpret_apdex(self, score: float) -> str:
        """Interpret Apdex score"""
        if score >= 0.94:
            return "Excellent"
        elif score >= 0.85:
            return "Good"
        elif score >= 0.70:
            return "Fair"
        elif score >= 0.50:
            return "Poor"
        else:
            return "Unacceptable"
    
    def _evaluate_performance(self, metrics: PerformanceMetrics) -> str:
        """Evaluate overall performance"""
        evaluations = []
        
        # Evaluate error rate
        if metrics.error_rate_percent < 0.1:
            evaluations.append("✓ Error rate is excellent (< 0.1%)")
        elif metrics.error_rate_percent < 1:
            evaluations.append("✓ Error rate is acceptable (< 1%)")
        elif metrics.error_rate_percent < 5:
            evaluations.append("⚠ Error rate is high (1-5%)")
        else:
            evaluations.append("✗ Error rate is unacceptable (> 5%)")
        
        # Evaluate p95 response time (assuming web application)
        if metrics.p95_response_time_ms < 1000:
            evaluations.append("✓ p95 response time is excellent (< 1s)")
        elif metrics.p95_response_time_ms < 2000:
            evaluations.append("✓ p95 response time is good (1-2s)")
        elif metrics.p95_response_time_ms < 3000:
            evaluations.append("⚠ p95 response time is acceptable (2-3s)")
        else:
            evaluations.append("✗ p95 response time is poor (> 3s)")
        
        # Evaluate Apdex
        if metrics.apdex_score >= 0.85:
            evaluations.append("✓ User experience is good (Apdex ≥ 0.85)")
        elif metrics.apdex_score >= 0.70:
            evaluations.append("⚠ User experience is fair (Apdex 0.70-0.85)")
        else:
            evaluations.append("✗ User experience is poor (Apdex < 0.70)")
        
        # Evaluate throughput stability (if we had multiple samples)
        # This would require more data
        
        return '\n'.join(evaluations)
    
    def create_visualization(self, metrics: PerformanceMetrics, output_file: str = None):
        """Create visualization of performance metrics"""
        fig, ((ax1, ax2), (ax3, ax4)) = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))
        fig.suptitle(f'Performance Analysis: {metrics.test_name}', fontsize=16)
        
        # 1. Response Time Distribution
        if metrics.response_times_ms:
            ax1.hist(metrics.response_times_ms, bins=50, alpha=0.7, color='skyblue')
            ax1.axvline(metrics.p95_response_time_ms, color='red', linestyle='--', 
                       label=f'p95: {metrics.p95_response_time_ms:.0f}ms')
            ax1.axvline(metrics.avg_response_time_ms, color='green', linestyle='--', 
                       label=f'Avg: {metrics.avg_response_time_ms:.0f}ms')
            ax1.set_xlabel('Response Time (ms)')
            ax1.set_ylabel('Frequency')
            ax1.set_title('Response Time Distribution')
            ax1.legend()
            ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # 2. Percentile Chart
        percentiles = [50, 90, 95, 99]
        percentile_values = [
            metrics.p50_response_time_ms,
            metrics.p90_response_time_ms,
            metrics.p95_response_time_ms,
            metrics.p99_response_time_ms
        ]
        bars = ax2.bar([str(p) for p in percentiles], percentile_values, color='lightcoral')
        ax2.set_xlabel('Percentile')
        ax2.set_ylabel('Response Time (ms)')
        ax2.set_title('Response Time Percentiles')
        ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Add value labels on bars
        for bar, value in zip(bars, percentile_values):
            height = bar.get_height()
            ax2.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 0.1,
                    f'{value:.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom')
        
        # 3. Success/Failure Pie Chart
        if metrics.total_requests > 0:
            labels = ['Successful', 'Failed']
            sizes = [metrics.successful_requests, metrics.failed_requests]
            colors = ['lightgreen', 'lightcoral']
            ax3.pie(sizes, labels=labels, colors=colors, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90)
            ax3.set_title(f'Request Success Rate (Total: {metrics.total_requests:,})')
        
        # 4. Metrics Summary
        summary_text = (
            f'Test Duration: {metrics.total_duration_seconds:.1f}s\n'
            f'Throughput: {metrics.throughput_rps:.1f} req/s\n'
            f'Error Rate: {metrics.error_rate_percent:.2f}%\n'
            f'Apdex Score: {metrics.apdex_score:.3f}\n'
            f'Apdex Rating: {self._interpret_apdex(metrics.apdex_score)}'
        )
        ax4.text(0.1, 0.5, summary_text, fontsize=12, verticalalignment='center')
        ax4.axis('off')
        ax4.set_title('Performance Summary')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        
        if output_file:
